job.title: Health and Wellbeing Coach
job.plain_text_description:
Are you passionate about helping people lead healthier, more active lives? Do you want to make a meaningful difference by reducing social isolation, improving mental wellbeing, and creating opportunities for people to connect within their local community?
If so, Fulham FC Foundation would love to hear from you.
We are seeking an enthusiastic, motivated, and committed Health & Wellbeing Coach to join our team on a 20 hour per week contract. Reporting to the Health & Wellbeing Manager, you will play a vital role in delivering high-quality sport, physical activity, and wellbeing programmes that positively influence people of all ages across our local communities.
Through your work, you will help participants improve their physical health and mental wellbeing, build confidence, and develop meaningful social connections. Our programmes use the power of sport and physical activity as a vehicle to create lasting change, with a focus on supporting healthier lifestyles and stronger, more connected communities.
As a Health & Wellbeing Coach, you will deliver a range of community-based activities designed to improve physical health, reduce loneliness and isolation, and support positive mental wellbeing. You will also work closely with local partners and stakeholders, helping to ensure our programmes deliver meaningful outcomes that extend beyond participation in sport and physical activity.
The successful candidate will have experience delivering football, sport, physical activity, or health improvement programmes within community settings, hold a minimum FA Introduction to Coaching Football (Level 1 equivalent) qualification, and demonstrate a strong commitment to the values and charitable mission of Fulham FC Foundation.
Our Health & Wellbeing programmes are delivered across Lambeth, Merton, Hammersmith & Fulham, Wandsworth, and Kingston. Sessions take place primarily on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, so we are looking for an individual who can travel independently across these boroughs and is available to work on these days.
Why Join Fulham FC Foundation?
At Fulham FC Foundation, we are committed to using the power of sport to transform lives and strengthen communities. By joining our team, you will:
• Work alongside a highly experienced, passionate, and supportive delivery team,
• Access a range of training and professional development opportunities,
• Continue to develop your coaching, facilitation, and community engagement skills,
• Play a key role in delivering life-changing programmes across South West London,
• Make a genuine difference to the lives of people within our local communities.
We strive for service excellence in everything we do and set high standards for all staff representing the Foundation. In return, we provide a supportive and inclusive environment where you can grow professionally while making a real and lasting impact on the people and communities we serve.
Further Information
Salary range is £13,500 - £14,000 for 20 hours per week.
Closing date for applications is 5.00pm on Friday 30th October 2026.
First stage interviews will take place in person on Friday 13th November at Craven Cottage. Please ensure you are available to interview on this date prior to applying.
Second stage interviews will be organised with individual candidates following the completion of the first stage interviews.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values. - To plan and deliver high-quality sessions to children, young people & adults in-line with FFCF standards. - To provide a safe, positive and inclusive environment at all times, - To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions. - To engage, include, inspire and grow participation across FFCF health & wellbeing activities. - To support the transition of participants between different FFCF programmes and activities. - To champion opportunities for individuals from underrepresented groups within FFCF activities. - To support the development of FFCF programmes through positive collaboration with internal departments and colleagues. - To support the promotion of all FFCF programmes across the local community. - To assist in data collection and completion of monitoring & evaluation on an ongoing basis.
*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
- Has experience delivering sport, physical activity, or health and wellbeing programmes within community settings
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Has a proven track record of maintaining the highest standards of safeguarding, health and safety, and quality assurance - Understands the importance of inclusion, participant welfare, and community engagement - Introduction to Coaching Football qualification - Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
- Shares our commitment to creating positive outcomes for participants and communities. - A positive role model. - Ability to travel independently across South-West London, including transport of equipment. - Well presented, with a professional manner. - Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants. - Excellent time-keeping & punctuality.Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.Demonstrates excellent communication and relationship-building skills
Preferred:
Experience:
- Working with vulnerable adults - Working for a Club Community Organisation (CCO). - Marketing & promoting participation activities in the community. - Delivery of sport or health & wellbeing activities specifically to females.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- FA Level 2/UEFA C in Coaching Football qualification (or higher). - Additional PE/HLTA qualification - Non-football NGB sports qualifications. - In-date FA Emergency First Aid (or willingness to work towards) - In-date FA Safeguarding Children certificate (or willingness to work towards)

job.title: CRM Marketing Manager
job.html_description:
Fulham FC is looking for an ambitious and analytical CRM Marketing Manager to play a key role in delivering the Club’s wider digital and data growth strategy. 

As guardian of the Club’s fan database, you will provide actionable insight and reporting to assist the Club in making informed decisions which support revenue generation across a range of commercial products, drive supporter engagement and acquisition.

The CRM Marketing Manager will own the the development of multichannel CRM marketing plans, audience segmentation and automated workflows, with the aim of serving existing fans and attracting new audiences with more personalised content and relevant experiences. 

Working across the Club’s digital estate, the role will be responsible for tracking user journeys, assess UX and improve conversion rates across owned and paid media chanels. 

You will work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure MarTech/CRM tools are effectively integrated, optimised, and evolved across the business, enabling us to maximise our understanding of the Fulham fan, align on business priorities and support growth.


Responsibilities

This role leads the management and development of CRM marketing tools and fan audience data, driving campaigns to support multiple departments including but not limited to marketing, ticketing, hospitality, retail and Fulham FC partners. 

Responsibilities include: 

•  Develop and deliver the Club’s fan data strategy focused on fan acquisition, engagement/retention, and commercial performance;
•  Ownership of the Fulham fan database and management of appointed MarTech/CRM systems and tools, including oversight for data integrations and hygiene;
•  Lead on supporter base insights, key market segments and KPIs; being a source of truth for FFC fan data, providing regular reporting on data size, quality and profiling, as well as recommendations for key target markets/potential commercial and acquisition opportunities;
•  Design, create and deploy automated, personalised and triggered multi-channel CRM marketing campigns – including audience segmentation, channel recommendations, execution and analysis: ensuring the right audiences are targeted with the right message across the right channel, at the right time;
•  Lead on data growth initiatives across all club touchpoints; track performance and adopt a ‘test and learn’ approach to improve acquisition/conversion, maximise communication effectiveness and reduce friction to further engagement;
•  Oversight of daily commercial sales to understand performance, run-rates and gaps, providing reccomendations to support growth;
•  Be a key support to the hospitality sales teams, implementing tools and features within CRM that improve efficiency and provide insight across sales and marketing, measuring the value of campaigns and support pipeline management;
•  Lead on Club audience research (e.g., surveys, focus groups);
•  Ensure marketing technology platforms are fully aligned with the Club’s broader data and technology ecosystem, working with the team to strengthen data insights;
•  Maintain the quality and integrity of customer data through regular audits, data cleaning, and deduplication processes.



Requirements

The CRM Marketing Manager must: 

•  Demonstrable experience working in CRM, marketing or lifecycle marketing, with a strong track record of delivering effective campaigns and commercial success;
•  Be comfortable working with large quantities of customer data and building audiences with MarTech/CRM tools;
•  Be confident to own CRM marketing activity from planning through to review and performance analytics;
•  Possess strong analytical skills, feeding actionable insight back to the business in a timely and accurate manner;
•  Be experienced in data segmentation and working across different channels, including email, SMS, app/push, website and paid media;
•  Be adaptable, organised and able to manage several projects at once;
•  Strong understanding of GDPR and UK data protection requirements;
•  Have a high attention to detail;
•  Excellent written and verbal communication skills – able to build strong relationships to work with internal and external stakeholders/suppliers. 

Ideally, the CRM Marketing Manager will: 

•  Have experiences of implementing/activating a CDP/CDXP system;
•  Have experience of using DotDigital or an equivalent MarTech/email platform;
•  Be experienced in managing user journeys across a single sign on (SSO) solution;
•  Be competent using Google Analytics;
•  Have experience of Microsoft Dynamics.

job.title: Billy the Badger
job.html_description:
Billy the Badger is a key component of Fulham Football Club’s identity and is involved across various Club events. As Billy the Badger, you will interact with the Club’s fan base across matchdays (FFC & FFCW), Foundation events, School visits and other adhoc activities.

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
 
  • Bring Billy the Badger to life through energetic, engaging and entertaining performances
  • Interact with supporters of all ages in a friendly, positive and approachable manner
  • Create memorable experiences for children, families and Fulham supporters
  • Attend home matchdays at Craven Cottage, including pre-match, half-time and post-match activities
  • Participate in photographs, videos, social media content and promotional campaigns
  • Support fan engagement activities, community events, club initiatives and special appearances
  • Work alongside the marketing, partnerships, women’s and Fulham FC Foundation teams
  • Respond creatively to the atmosphere and events of the matchday while staying true to Billy's character
  • Follow agreed performance, safety and operational guidelines
  • Maintain a professional appearance and positive attitude while representing Fulham FC
  • Be prepared to perform for extended periods and work in a physically demanding costume

Requirements

Fulham Football Club is looking for an enthusiastic, energetic and charismatic individual to bring Billy the Badger to life and help create unforgettable experiences for supporters of all ages.
 
As Billy the Badger, you will be a key part of the matchday experience at Craven Cottage, entertaining fans, interacting with supporters and representing the Club at matches, community activities, promotional events and other appearances.
 
This is a highly visible role that requires someone who can communicate through personality, movement and humour while maintaining the character of Billy the Badger at all times.

job.title: Academy Therapist (Casual)
job.html_description:
To deliver high-quality physiotherapy services across the Foundation Phase (FP) and Youth Development Phase (YDP) squads (U9–U16) within a multidisciplinary team environment. Provide medical support on match days, during clinics, and at tournaments, ensuring optimal care and performance outcomes for academy players. Assist in the implementation of injury prevention strategies and rehabilitation programmes aimed at maximising performance, enhancing recovery, and minimising injury risk. Support the effective transition of players from the FP and YDP into the Professional Development Phase (PDP) by contributing to a comprehensive and cohesive medical pathway.

Responsibilities

The therapist will play a key role in the delivery of medical services to academy players across the Foundation and Youth Development Phases. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, they will support all aspects of injury management, contribute to player development through preventative care strategies, and ensure effective communication and documentation across all stakeholders.

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
 • Provide medical cover for FP and YDP players during match days (primarily Sundays, with some midweek fixtures), evening clinics, and domestic or international tournaments. 
  • Support the assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation of injuries in collaboration with the full-time U9–U16 physiotherapist, ensuring appropriate return-to-play protocols are followed. 
  • Contribute to the planning and delivery of injury prevention strategies, including individual and group-based sessions tailored to player needs. 
  • Liaise effectively with coaching staff to support player load management during key stages of physical development. 
  • Communicate and coordinate with parents, external medical providers (NHS/private), and internal staff to facilitate appropriate ongoing care. 
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date medical records on the PMA system and ensure clear handovers between staff for all FP and YDP players. 
  • Assist in the transition of players from FP/YDP into the PDP phase by sharing relevant medical and movement history with appropriate personnel. 
  • Engage in internal CPD, contribute to research and development within paediatric sports medicine, and undertake relevant professional development to support continuous improvement.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Therapist must:
  • BSc degree in Physiotherapy, Sports Therapy, Sports Rehabilitation. 
  • Be a member of the appropriate governing body – CSP, SST, BASRaT 
  • FA Level 4 ITMMiF • Experience working in a sports medicine environment.
  • Experience working in a multidisciplinary team. 
  • FA Safegurading • Be able to work as part of a team 
  • Available to work on a flexible basis including evening and weekends

Ideally, the Casual Academy Therapist will:
  • FA Level 5 ATMMiF
  • Experience and understanding of paediatric sports medicine 
  • Experience working within a Category 1 football academy

job.title: Warehouse Operative/Driver (Part-time)
job.plain_text_description:
Oversee the efficient receipt, storage, dispatch and movements of all stock. Be able to ensure productivity targets are achieved and that all warehouse processes are running smoothly and promptly. Delivering of Stock to the store.
This role is 24 hours per week: shifts on Monday, Tuesday and Friday.
Responsibilities
Below are example responsibilities but this is not intended to be an exhaustive list:

Key Skills:
- A strong communication skill at all levels both oral and written - Strong interpersonal skills and confidence in dealing with people at all levels of the organisation - Pragmatic and flexible approach - Work well under pressure through very busy trading periods - Team player with a hands-on approach - Know how to do Shirt printings - The ability to drive a van for delivery purposes

job.title: Lead Academy Performance Coach (U9-16)
job.html_description:
As Lead Academy Performance Coach (U9-U16) you will be responsible for both the wider physical performance strategy in the FP and YDP and performance support for select YDP age-groups.

This is both a coaching and leadership position that requires you to have combined experience as an applied practitioner and leading a team of performance coaches to implement physical performance strategies.

Preferable, you will also have experience in both applied sport science and strength and conditioning in a youth development programme.

The role will also work in collaboration with the HoP, Lead Academy Physiotherapist, Lead Academy Strength and Conditioning Coach and Lead Academy Performance Coach (PDP), to identify innovative practice to develop the programme.

Responsibilities

Essential Requirements
  • Minimum of 3 years' experience working with elite athletes, specifically aged 9-16.
  • CASES accreditation.
  • UKSCA accreditation.
  • Experience working within a multidisciplinary team.
  • BSc degree in a relevant subject area.
  • Relevant professional body accreditation.
  • Knowledge of professional development strategies.
  • FA Safeguarding certification.
  • Emergency First Aid certification (or equivalent).
  • Honest, humble and hard-working approach.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
  • Respectful and professional in all interactions.
  • Reliable with a strong work ethic.
  • Well organised with effective time management skills.
  • Demonstrable leadership skills.

Desirable Requirements
  • Minimum of 1 year's experience working with elite athletes aged 9-16 within a Category 1 Academy.
  • Experience leading a physical development programme.
  • MSc degree in a relevant subject area.
  • Ability to make effective decisions under pressure.
  • Demonstrated resilience and ability to deal positively with adversity.
  • Willingness to accept responsibility and accountability for actions and decisions.

Requirements

• Assist HoP with the production, implementation, and monitoring of the Performance Department Plan in line with the Academy Performance Plan and EPPP requirements. 
• Provide industry leading performance support to select YDP age-groups. 
• Implement a clear physical development strategy within the FP and YDP that is integrated with the Performance Department Plan and aligned with the wider MDT.  
• Oversee the design, delivery and tracking of YDP strength and conditioning. 
• Manage the monitoring and reporting of the YDP readiness to train. 
• In collaboration with HoP set, monitor and review Academy Performance Department targets. 
• Oversee the design, delivery and tracking of YDP GPS data and reporting. 
• Facilitate regular dialogue within staff delivering the physical performance strategy to the FP and YDP. 
• Liaise with the YDP MDT to effectively periodise and individual player schedules at the macro, meso and microcycle and play. 
• Collaborate with the MDT to create player profiles and play an active role in player review cycles.
• Lead on internal and external physical performance testing within the YDP. 
• Ensure effective communication and planning between the Lead Academy Performance Coach (PDP) and U18 Performance staff on player transition of incoming scholars. 
• Assist in performance support with the PDP. 
• Ensure all FP and YDP performance staff understand and can clearly convey the department philosophy, plans and targets as directed by HoP. 
• Lead on collecting, tracking and reporting of growth and maturation data.
• Build good relationships with senior management, heads of department and wider academy staff to help facilitate consolidated working practices across the academy. 
• Liaise with medical staff to effectively design and deliver late-stage rehab in the YDP. 
• Under direction from the HoP, contribute to the design and execution of research projects to improve sport science practice. 
• Liaise with PDP staff on transition player programming and development. 
• Support, where required, Academy events including inductions and workshops. 
• Lead on recruitment for FP and YDP performance team  
• Assist HoP with Performance Department administrative duties. • Lead on long-term CPD for FP and YDP performance staff 
• Uphold the highest Safeguarding standards.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on Friday 6th November, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

• Support, where required, Academy events including inductions and workshops.
• Lead on recruitment for FP and YDP performance team
• Assist HoP with Performance Department administrative duties. • Lead on long-term CPD for FP and YDP performance staff
• Uphold the highest Safeguarding standards.
Benefits
We expect to close applications on Friday 6th November, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: Fire Officer
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 

 

The Fire Team will not normally be expected to be involved in the management of spectators. When deployed as a member of the Fire Team the primary is one of fire prevention and first response should an outbreak of fire occur.
This role is suitable for candidates who are or have experience of the fire industry or stewards who are willing to undergo additional fire safety training to enable them to carry out this role.

Responsibilities

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as dictated by the Head of Safety.
  • Undertake pre-match and post-match fire checks as instructed by the Fire Team leader. Arrive at Steward Sign as directed.
  • Conduct Pre-Match Checks and specified documentation on Raven Controls as required.
  • Conduct patrols within the stand and under croft’s to minimise the risk of fire breaking out and assisting to prevent the spread of fire. 
  • Respond to Fire and associated incidents as directed by FFC Control, ensuring staff are supported, appropriate action is taken, and that information is passed to the Safety Management Team in FFC Control (Act – Inform – Escalate)
  • Attend during match meetings with Fire Team leader for the identification of issues to be addressed, learning points and review of specific deployments. 
  • Report any fire safety concerns to the fire team leader for appropriate action and escalation to FFC Control and the Safety Officer. 
  • Know the location of and be able to effectively operate the firefighting equipment at the Stadium. 
  • Be able to provide basic ‘First Aid’ if required. 
  • Know the location of the First Aid Rooms located within the Stadium. 
  • Be fully conversant with any methods or messages used to alert staff that an emergency has arisen. 
  • Be capable of recognising potential fire hazards and items of interest or suspect packages, reporting such matters immediately to the Fire Team leader, a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, or Safety Officer. 
  • Promptly comply with any instruction given by a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, Safety Officer, or Police Officer. 
  • Comply with the relevant instructions and guidance contained in the Stewards Handbook and standing instructions for the FFC Fire Team. 
  • Attend all required training. 
  • To understand their general responsibilities towards the health and safety and welfare of all spectators, other stewards, staff, and themselves.


Essential and Desirable 
 
Background in Fire industry (present/previous Fire Service) and willing to undergo relevant training. 

Requirements

To act in accordance with the general recommendations of the Guide to Safety at Sports Ground (Green Guide) and the specific requirements of the Safety Certificate issued by the Local Authority under the Safety of Sports Ground Act 1975. Fire Safety Officers play a key role in the event day safety team ensuring that the stadium provides a safe and secure environment for thousands of visitors. You will become a focal point for all fire safety issues, providing preventative advice and measures in an emergency.

 

  • You should be a minimum of 18 years of age, be fit, active and have the character and temperament to carry out the duties required. 
  • You should possess good communication skills.
  • You must be able to attend most first-team home fixtures and other major events held at the stadium.
  • You should be polite, courteous, and helpful to all supporters.
  • Whilst on duty you will adhere to the Club dress code and be clean and tidy.
  • You are not engaged to watch the game but are expected to concentrate on your area of responsibility. 
  • You should never show hostility or use obscene or offensive language to any supporters.
  • You should never act in any way likely to bring discredit on the Club.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach - DisAbility
job.plain_text_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the casual position of DisAbility Football & Sports Coach.
Reporting directly to our Senior DisAbility Development Manager, the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches are responsible for delivering high-quality football & sports coaching to children, young people and adults with disabilities and additional needs. This role involves delivery across a wide-range of our DisAbility Programmes, including Pan DisAbility Clubs, Active Autism, Down’s Syndrome ‘Badgers’, Blind and Partially Sighted, Cerebral Palsy and Dwarfism Football Sessions. In addition there will be opportunities to work in our DisAbility Schools programme delivering PE, Enrichment Activities and After School Clubs.
While the primary focus of this role is on DisAbility Football & Sport, there may be opportunities to contribute to other FFC Foundation activities such as Skills Club, Development Centres, Soccer Schools, Primary Education, Kicks, and Health & Wellbeing. We would encourage candidates to prioritise DisAbility Programmes where possible, while remaining flexible to support other areas as needed.
This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the role necessitates involvement in supporting the delivery of programme activities as and when required.
The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience delivering football & sports coaching sessions to children & young people with disabilities or additional needs in grassroots & school settings, holds at least a FA Level 1/Introduction to Coaching Football qualification and is committed to the charitable purpose of Fulham FC Foundation.
As this role is casual, there is no set timetable. Sessions may be offered on an adhoc or regular basis, depending on the needs of Fulham FC Foundation. It is the responsibility of the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to maintain consistent and effective communication with our Senior DisAbility Development Manager and Operations Officers to ensure the continuation of work.
Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to accept, work. DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time, will be deactivated.
The successful candidates should be available to work across at least one of the below times, in order to receive work. We are extremely keen to hear from those who are able to work on Saturday mornings.
Weekdays – 9am to 5 pm;
Weekday Evenings – 5pm to 9pm
Weekends – Saturdays – 8am to 12noon.
Work in other timings is available, however on a far reduced frequency.
Salary Range: £12.95 p/h to £16.50 p/h
Next steps
:
There is no closing date for this role. Applications will be reviewed on a bi-weekly basis.
If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences
*
This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation
.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values. - To plan and deliver high-quality football and sports coaching sessions to children, young people & adults in-line with FFCF standards. - To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times, - To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions. - To engage, include, inspire and grow participation across FFCF activities. - To support the transition of participants between different FFCF programmes and activities. - To champion opportunities for individuals from underrepresented groups within FFCF activities. - To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people. - To support the development of FFCF programmes through positive collaboration with Department Managers / Operations Officers. - To support the promotion of FFCF programmes across the local community. - To assist in data collection and completion of monitoring & evaluation on an ongoing basis.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
- Delivery of football coaching sessions in a grassroots environment - Delivery of sports coaching sessions to children, young people or adults with disabilities and additional needs. - Delivery within a school/college setting. - Working in a customer-facing role.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Introduction to Coaching Football qualification - In-date FA Emergency First Aid - In-date FA Safeguarding Children certificate - Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
- A positive role-model for children & young people. - Ability to travel independently across South-West London, including transport of equipment. - Well presented, with a professional manner. - Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants. - Excellent time-keeping & punctuality. - Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.
Preferred:
Experience:
- Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions in a Club Community Organisation (CCO). - Delivery of Physical Education within a school setting. - Delivery within a classroom environment. - Marketing & Promoting participation activities in the community. - Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions to females.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- FA Level 2/UEFA C in Coaching Football qualification (or higher). - Additional PE/HLTA qualification - Mentoring qualification - Non-football NGB sports qualifications.

job.title: Matchday Retail Assistant
job.html_description:
Position Purpose

This role involves supporting the day-to-day operations of the Club’s retail store, delivering excellent customer service, maintaining high standards of presentation, and ensuring efficient stock handling and sales processes.

Responsibilities

Essential and Desirable

  • Strong customer service and communication skills, with the ability to assist customers in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Able to work effectively in a fast-paced retail environment, both independently and as part of a team, while maintaining high standards of organisation and efficiency.
  • Available to work all home matchdays - weekends and evenings including bank holidays.
  • Adaptability to handle a variety of situations

Ideally, Matchday Retail Assistant will:
  • Previous EPOS experience
  • Retail Experience

Requirements

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
• Provide excellent and helpful customer service, assisting customers with products and purchases.
• Operate the till and process card payments accurately.
• Print names and numbers onto replica shirts, ensuring customer orders are completed correctly and to a high standard.
• Replenish stock and keep stores and displays tidy and well-presented.
• Price and label products correctly across the store.
• Support the matchday running of the store and assist with additional tasks when required
• Work in various units across the stadium

job.title: Safety Steward
job.html_description:
The role is one of customer care and they will be expected to call on a supervisor or specialist stewards for assistance in dealing with breaches of Ground Regulations. 
In house stewards may be asked to undertake searching at the turnstiles as directed.

Responsibilities

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as dictated by Head of Safety.
  • Attend a pre-event briefing and ensure all information is understood.  
  • Do not leave the Stadium after ‘signing in’ until the end of your duties. 
  • Undertake pre-match and post-match stand checks.  
  • To always be responsible for the safety and comfort of spectators within a designated area. 
  • Carry out pre match and post-match safety checks as instructed by Supervisor.  
  • To staff entrances, exits and other key safety points within the Stadium. 
  • Constantly monitor the spectators in your area checking for signs of distress or overcrowding and act in accordance with standing instructions. 
  • Assist in the prevention of overcrowding by ensuring the crowd limits in various parts of the ground are complied with. 
  • To control and direct spectators entering and leaving the Stadium and to assist in this movement.  
  • Ensure that gangways and exit/evacuation routes in your area are kept clear. 
  • Identify and investigate any incident or occurrence among spectators reporting findings to a supervisor. Where appropriate complete the relevant Incident/Offence Report.  
  • Enforce and immediately report any breach of the Ground Regulations to Supervisor. 
  • Know the location of and be able to effectively operate the firefighting equipment at the Stadium.  
  • Be able to provide basic First Aid if required. 
  • Know the location of the First Aid Rooms located within the Stadium.  
  • Be fully conversant with any methods or messages used to alert staff that an emergency has arisen. 
  • Be capable of recognising potential fire hazards and items of interest or suspect packages, reporting such matters immediately to a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer or Safety Officer.  
  • Promptly comply with any instruction given by a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, Safety Officer or Police Officer. 
  • Remain at allocated post as instructed unless authorised or ordered to do otherwise by a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, Safety Officer, or Police Officer.  
  • Report immediately to a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer or Safety Officer any damage or defect which is likely to pose a threat or danger to spectator safety eg damaged seat or barrier. 
  • Assist as required in the evacuation of spectators etc from the Stadium.  
  • Comply with the relevant instructions and guidance contained in the Stewards Handbook. 
  • To undertake specific duties in an emergency or as directed by the Safety Officer, Deputy Safety Officer or the appropriate emergency services officer. 
  • Attend debriefs at the conclusion of the match and conduct thorough sweeps of the stands. 
  • Attend all required training.  
  • To understand their general responsibilities towards the health and safety and welfare of all spectators, other stewards ground staff and themselves 

Requirements

  • You should be a minimum of 18 years of age, be fit, active and have the character and temperament to carry out the duties of a Steward. 
  • You should possess good communication skills and be of sound character.
  • You must be able to attend most first-team home fixtures and other major events held at the stadium.
  • You should be polite, courteous and helpful to all supporters.
  • Whilst on duty you will adhere to the Club dress code and be clean and tidy.
  • You are not engaged to watch the game but are expected to concentrate on your area of responsibility. 
  • You will not wear team colours whilst on duty. You should not, whilst on duty, eat, drink or smoke in view of the public.
  • You should not consume alcohol before or during a tour of duty.
  • You should never celebrate the team scoring a goal. 
  • You should never show hostility or use obscene or offensive language to any supporters.
  • You should never act in any way likely to bring discredit on the Club.

job.title: Chef De Partie
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 
 

  • We are looking for a chef with a background in catering for professional sports teams to join our passionate nutrition focused team.

  • You will support our Head Chef and Sous Chef in providing balanced, nutritional and high quality meals to our players and support staff at the training ground.

  • A good basis of nutrition helps our players to achieve their individual nutritional goals, ultimately enhancing health, recovery and performance.

  • To lead the kitchen team in preparing and providing meals to our youth and women teams.

  • Some travel with teams to away games may be necessary, following their weekly schedule/fixtures, ensuring all food provided to them meets the presentation, taste and performance need of the group.

Requirements

Requirements and Responsibilities
 

  • Work with the Head Chef and independently to create and develop exciting seasonal menus. 

  • Prepare meals for youth and women teams working within the nutritional guidelines and ensure junior team members are working correctly to achieve this with you.

  • Instruct junior team members accordingly to ensure youth and women teams' meals are delivered on time and presented to a high standard.

  • Support and lead junior members of the kitchen team.

  • Check stock requirements and order accordingly in the Head/Sous chef absence.

  • Travel with teams in the UK and abroad when required as the catering team representative and provide food provisions as requested.

  • Assist in the preparation of all travel food requirements whilst displaying good organisational skills.

  • Support Head/Sous chef to deliver constantly high quality food in a timely manner.

  • Cover Sous chefs' role as and when required.

  • Working closely with the Supervisor to ensure the highest level of food safety and hygiene are maintained. Compliance with COSHH.

  • Flexibility to work around the teams schedules.



Essential and Desirable
 

The Chef De Partie must have: 

  • Minimum of 1 year experience providing food to sports teams/athletes
  • Level 2 NVQ Professional Cookery or equivalent
  • Excellent communication skill to lead the junior kitchen team
  • Works well under pressure with the ability to remain calm with last minute schedule changes
 
Ideally, the Chef De Partie will: 
  • Football specific experience
  • Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate
  • Performance nutrition knowledge

job.title: Casual Mini-Bus Driver
job.html_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the position of Casual Mini-Bus Driver for the Foundation. 

Reporting directly to our Football & Education Head Coaches the Casual Mini-Bus Driver is responsible for providing a safe, reliable and professional driving service for the Foundation’s Football & Education Programme. The successful candidate will be responsible for transporting our Football & Education teams safely to and from fixtures, competitions, training sessions and other programme-related activities. The role will require you to drive a 17-seater or larger minibus. 

This is a zero-hour contract with no guaranteed hours or working times, with work being offered based on the programme’s fixtures and activity schedule. The majority of these journeys will take place on Tuesday’s, Wednesday’s and Thursday’s. There may also be occasional requirements on Mondays and Fridays, depending on the fixture schedule. Most of these hours will be during the working day (9am – 5pm) however with some longer away games you may be required outside of these times. Therefore, flexibility is required for the role with some work being offered at relatively short notice. These hours will also predominantly take place during term time, with only the occasional need for drivers during the school holiday. 

The successful candidate will be someone who holds a D1 entitlement on their driving licence, has experience driving a minibus, and would be comfortable working with young people. You will also be required to hold an up-to-date DBS check and complete your FA Safeguarding and First Aid Training.  

Salary Range: £15ph 

Next steps: 
If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences.

*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation.


Responsibilities

  • Safely transport Football & Education participants and staff to and from fixtures, training sessions, competitions and other programme activities.
 
  • Plan journeys effectively, allowing sufficient time to account for traffic and potential delays.
 
  • Complete pre-use vehicle safety checks before each journey and report any defects immediately.
 
  • Maintain a valid D1 entitlement and cooperate with periodic DVLA licence checks as part of the Club's fleet compliance process.
 
  • Ensure all passengers follow appropriate safety procedures, including the use of seatbelts.
 
  • Follow all relevant road traffic legislation, and internal policies and procedures, such as (but not limited to) our fuel card and vehicle usage procedures.
 
  • Comply with the Club's Fleet Policy and all vehicle-related procedures.
 
  • Ensure vehicles are returned in a clean, tidy and roadworthy condition, with keys returned in line with Club procedures.
 
  • Communicate effectively with Football & Education staff regarding collection times, destinations, delays and any issues arising during journeys.
 
  • Report any accidents, incidents, damages, defects, near misses, or safeguarding concerns in accordance with organisational procedures.
 
  • Always represent Fulham Football Club and Fulham FC Foundation to a high standard in line with club values at all times.

Requirements

Essential: 
Experience: 
•  Proven experience of driving a minibus, ideally a 17-seater or larger vehicle.
•  Experience transporting passengers in a professional or organised setting.
•  Planning journeys effectively, allowing sufficient time to account for traffic and potential delays.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
•  A full, clean UK driving licence with D1 entitlement to legally drive the required minibus.
•  A good understanding of UK road safety and relevant driving regulations.
•  The ability to work independently and manage journeys effectively.

Personal Qualities:
•  Excellent reliability, punctuality and timekeeping.
•  Good communication skills and a professional manner.
•  A flexible approach to working hours and availability.
•  The ability to work appropriately and professionally around young people.

Preferred: 
Experience: 
•  Previous experience working within football, sport, education, charity or youth programmes.
•  Previous experience transporting young people or students.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
•  FA First Aid & Safeguarding 
•  Ability to interact with others in a positive manner
•  Strong understanding of the local area
•  Driver Certificate of Professional Competence (Driver CPC)

- Maintain a valid D1 entitlement and cooperate with periodic DVLA licence checks as part of the Club's fleet compliance process.
- Ensure all passengers follow appropriate safety procedures, including the use of seatbelts.
- Follow all relevant road traffic legislation, and internal policies and procedures, such as (but not limited to) our fuel card and vehicle usage procedures.
- Comply with the Club's Fleet Policy and all vehicle-related procedures.
- Ensure vehicles are returned in a clean, tidy and roadworthy condition, with keys returned in line with Club procedures.
- Communicate effectively with Football & Education staff regarding collection times, destinations, delays and any issues arising during journeys.
- Report any accidents, incidents, damages, defects, near misses, or safeguarding concerns in accordance with organisational procedures.
- Always represent Fulham Football Club and Fulham FC Foundation to a high standard in line with club values at all times.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
• Proven experience of driving a minibus, ideally a 17-seater or larger vehicle.
• Experience transporting passengers in a professional or organised setting.
• Planning journeys effectively, allowing sufficient time to account for traffic and potential delays.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
• A full, clean UK driving licence with D1 entitlement to legally drive the required minibus.
• A good understanding of UK road safety and relevant driving regulations.
• The ability to work independently and manage journeys effectively.
Personal Qualities:
• Excellent reliability, punctuality and timekeeping.
• Good communication skills and a professional manner.
• A flexible approach to working hours and availability.
• The ability to work appropriately and professionally around young people.
Preferred:
Experience:
• Previous experience working within football, sport, education, charity or youth programmes.
• Previous experience transporting young people or students.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
• FA First Aid & Safeguarding
• Ability to interact with others in a positive manner
• Strong understanding of the local area
• Driver Certificate of Professional Competence (Driver CPC)

job.title: Casual Academy Scout (Midlands)
job.html_description:
The National Academy scouting team is responsible for identifying and monitoring players either from grassroots or other Academies in national regions. They will complete reports on players and share information with other Academy staff to develop a range of player intelligence across the local area. 

There is a particular interest for us to recruit within the following teams: 
- Grassroots – Midlands 
- Academy- Midlands

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
• To manage your individual weekend schedule and regularly attend fixtures within your region or
across your phase.
• To complete reports on players all players with potential across your region and phase.
• Network with other national scouts to share information on potential target players.
• To keep National and department Managers informed of high potential players across their area or
age phase.
• To support with the ongoing communication to the families of players within our TID programmes
and on trial as and when required.
• To support the delivery of Talent ID programmes and events as and when required.
• Participate in scouting team meetings to further discuss succession planning and their identified
target players.
• To attend department meetings and participate in all CPD and required safeguarding training when
appropriate.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) must have:
• Knowledge and networks within the local area they scout.
• Previous experience scouting for another Academy (Cat 1, 2 or 3)
• FA Talent ID Level 2
• FA Safeguarding

Ideally, the Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) will:
• Previous experience scouting for another Cat 1 Academy.
• FA Level 2 Coaching
• Full Driver’s License

job.title: Matchday Groundsperson Casual
job.html_description:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:

• Repair works to the pitch in the form of divoting after warm up’s, half time and post-match use.
• Post-match pedestrian mowing using rotary and cylinder mowers.
• Setting up grow lights and moving them from storage compound into stadium post-game when required.
• Washing and cleaning of machinery after usage.
• Comply with all Health and Safety regulations and requirements within the Company and your role.
• Drive vehicles and handle equipment as required for grounds maintenance operations.
• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with managers, colleagues and end users, ensure grounds management are kept informed of any issues that may be identified.
• Undertaking general maintenance operations associated with pitch.
• Work within a stadium team to ensure the upkeep of the stadium pitch.
• This job description does not contain all the duties and responsibilities that may arise in this role, you will need to undertake other duties as instructed and use initiative to ensure the safe operational functioning of the stadium.
• Expectation is to work at least 75% of home fixtures.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach – Team Coaching
job.html_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the position of a Casual Football & Sports Coach – Team Coaching

Reporting directly to our Operations Officers, this role would involve both the management of these teams, as well as providing high-quality, team-based training sessions throughout the week. You will also be responsible for overseeing any fixtures these team have across the season. 

This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the delivery of training sessions and fixtures changes across the school term.

The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience managing a team, and holds at least a UEFA C License qualification.

Although this role is casual, with the hours varying across the season, meaning that there is no set timetable. There are some key times when training sessions and fixtures are likely to happen. 

Therefore, the ideal candidate will have good availability during the afternoons of the working week. 

The ideal availability will be:
Monday – Friday from 2pm to 6pm

There will also be opportunity to work across other foundation programmes such as our ‘Player Development Centres’ and ‘Girls Development Centres’ should the successful candidate want to.

Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for Football Coaches to accept, work. Football Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time (3 months), may no longer be offered work.

Responsibilities

  • To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values.
  • To design and deliver high quality, team training sessions to the teams you’ll be working with. 
  • To manage the teams during both home and away fixtures, including all the team admin that does along with managing the team.
  • To provide high-quality, individualised feedback to each of the players in your teams to support their footballing development.
  • To be a positive role model to the student athletes, helping both motivate and support them with their football, and education.
  • To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people.
  • To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times,
  • To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions.

Requirements

Essential

Experience:
  • Experience of delivering high quality training sessions to footballers.
  • Experience of running a 9 or 11 aside football team.
  • Experience of working with others as part of a coaching team.
  • Has a driving license and/or is willing to travel independently.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
  • Excellent verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent knowledge of Football[AS1] .
  • Excellent knowledge of the pathway opportunities for players.
  • First Aid, Safeguarding and DBS qualification.
  • A UEFA C Coaching Qualification, or currently undertaking and due to complete this year.
  • Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
  • A positive role-model for children & young people.
  • Ability to travel independently across Surrey and South-West London, including transport of equipment.
  • Well presented, with a professional manner.
  • Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants.
  • Excellent time-keeping & punctuality.
  • Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.
 
Preferred

Experience:
  • Experience of delivering football sessions in a secondary school
  • Experience of working with high performing footballers.
  • Experience of leading local grassroots [AS2] team
 Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
  • Additional football qualifications such as Goalkeeping, S&C, or Fitness.
  • Knowledge and links to local grassroots football teams.
  • UEFA B License (or willing to work towards)

job.title: Kitchen Porter
job.html_description:
To assist the Kitchen and Front of house staff in cleaning of all kitchen items, equipment,
machinery, floors and surfaces. Maintaining high standards and safe practices in all areas.
This is generally a Monday to Friday role however some flexibility with working hours will be

Responsibilities

Essential

  • Good command of the English language

  • Likes to get stuck in

job.title: Casual Physiotherapist
job.html_description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and organised Physiotherapist to join the Fulham FC Foundation team, working in a casual capacity to support our ‘Football & Education’ teams. The successful candidate will provide injury assessment, treatment and rehabilitation services through a weekly clinic and deliver pitch-side medical support on matchdays.

This role will have two key responsibilities that will support our ‘Football & Education Programme’ to maximise player performance, enhance recovery, reduce injury risk, and minimise the risk to players during a pitch side medical emergency.

The successful candidates first responsibility will be providing a weekly injury clinic to our participants to make sure they are receiving correct treatment and advice to minimise any potential injuries. As well as supporting the coaching team to make sure that any injuries caused due to training methods are minimised.

Although this role is casual, with the hours varying across the season, meaning that there is no set timetable. There are some key times when the injury clinic and fixtures will occur. Therefore, the ideal candidate will have good availability during the late morning/early afternoons of the working week. Please be aware that some away fixtures will take up the majority of the working day.
Salary: £25 p/h


Responsibilities

Responsibilities will include:
· Deliver a weekly two-hour physiotherapy clinic for injured players.
· Assess, diagnose and treat football-related injuries.
· Develop and monitor rehabilitation programmes.
· Provide injury prevention advice and education.
· Maintain accurate treatment and injury records.

The role's second responsibility will be to provide medical and emergency support during match days across both our male and female teams. This responsibility will include:

· Attend designated fixtures as required.
· Provide pitch-side assessment and injury management.
· Deliver first aid and emergency medical care where necessary.
· Ensure medical equipment and supplies are maintained.

Requirements

The successful candidate must have an excellent knowledge of rehabilitation and injury prevention, with extensive experience of delivering these within a sporting background. You will also be expected to have experience of providing medical support during match days, and of having excellent organisation and communication skills to support the wider coaching team.

The following qualifications, skills and experience are essential:
· FA Intermediate Trauma Medical Management in Football certificate or equivalent first aid qualification. – Could get away with PHCIS Level 2.
· BSc in Physiotherapy or Sport Rehabilitation
· Sports Trauma Management or Emergency Aid in Sport qualification.

job.title: Video & Content Officer
job.plain_text_description:
The Video & Content Officer will be responsible for creating compelling visual content that showcases the impact of Fulham FC Foundation's work. The role will lead on videography and content creation across the Foundation's programmes, events and campaigns.
Working closely with delivery teams and the Communications Manager, the postholder will capture and share engaging stories that increase participation, attract supporters and partners, and demonstrate community impact.
Why Join Fulham FC Foundation?
At Fulham FC Foundation, we are committed to using the power of sport to transform lives and strengthen communities. By joining our team, you will:
• Work alongside a highly experienced, passionate, and supportive delivery team,
• Access a range of training and professional development opportunities,
• Continue to develop your coaching, facilitation, and community engagement skills,
• Play a key role in delivering life-changing programmes across South West London,
• Make a genuine difference to the lives of people within our local communities.
We strive for service excellence in everything we do and set high standards for all staff representing the Foundation. In return, we provide a supportive and inclusive environment where you can grow professionally while making a real and lasting impact on the people and communities we serve.
Further Information
Salary range is £27,000 - £28,500 for 40 hours per week.
​
Please note: closing date for applications is 25th October.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values.
Videography and Content Production
• Plan, capture and edit video content for promotional, fundraising, programme and impact campaigns.
• Produce engaging short-form and long-form video content suitable for digital and social media platforms.
• Develop creative concepts and storyboards aligned with campaign objectives.
• Support regular video review and planning meetings to ensure content quality and consistency.
Storytelling and Impact Content
• Lead the planning, filming, editing and delivery of participant case study videos.
• Work directly with programme teams and beneficiaries to identify compelling stories.
• Ensure all content is captured and produced in line with safeguarding, consent and brand guidelines.
Photography
• Support on the capture of high-quality photography from Foundation programmes, events, campaigns and community activities.
• Maintain a comprehensive library of images for future communications and marketing use.
• Edit and optimise photographic content for digital, print and social media channels.
Marketing Support
• Provide ad hoc multimedia and creative support for communications and marketing campaigns. • Assist with content requirements for fundraising, events and partnership activations.
*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
• Experience in professional videography and photography.
• Experience producing content for social media, websites and digital marketing campaigns.
• Experience editing video and photographic assets.
• Experience interviewing and developing feature videos.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud applications, including Premiere Pro, Photoshop and Lightroom. - Strong storytelling and content-writing skills. - Excellent planning and organisational abilities. - Ability to work independently while managing multiple projects. - Strong interpersonal skills and confidence when engaging with programme participants.
Desirable
- Experience within sport, education, youth work, charity or community sectors. - Knowledge of social media content trends and platform best practice. - Understanding of safeguarding and consent processes when working with children and vulnerable adults.

job.title: u18 Head Coach
job.html_description:
We are seeking an experienced and passionate coach to play a key role in delivering and enhancing our Academy Performance Plan. The successful candidate will be responsible for planning, delivering and reviewing high-quality coaching activities that support the individual development needs of Academy players. Working across the player pathway, they will help ensure smooth and effective transitions from the U16 age group into the Professional Development Phase and from the U18s into the U21 programme, maintaining consistency in player development. The role will also contribute to the ongoing development of the Academy Performance Plan and Technical Plan, helping to drive continuous improvement and maximise player potential.

Responsibilities

The U18 Head Coach must hold or have:
  • Experience of coaching adolescents in a Category 1 and/or Premier League Academy setting.
  • Experience of supporting parents/carers of adolescents within similar settings.
  • Experience of delivering individual player development programmes (ILPs/IDPs) within a multi-disciplinary environment.
  • Hold appropriate and up to date qualifications to conform to Professional Game Academy Audit Company (PGAAC) and Premier League Youth Development Rules (PLYDR) requirements.
  • UEFA A Licence (FA Level 4 qualification), and remain up to date with associated CPD requirements.
  • FA Advanced Youth Award (FA Level 4 qualification).
  • Valid FA Introduction to First Aid in Football certificate.
  • Valid FA Safeguarding Children certificate.
  • Broad awareness of the football industry’s governing policies and youth football protocols, in particular the Premier League’s Youth Development Rules.
  • Knowledge of regulations, research and expected practices in relation to working with adolescents, with particular reference to safeguarding, well-being, social development and safety.
  • Be player/person-centred (individualised) in approach to development.
  • Have high-level interpersonal skills, including being an effective and adaptable communicator.
  • Demonstrate resilience towards the everyday rigours of high-performance environments.
  • Be diligent, hard-working, detail-driven and intrinsically motivated by the Academy’s mission.
  • Hold a forward-thinking, positive and optimistic mindset.
  • Be willing to hold honest and supportive conversations with parents, guardians or carers of Academy players.
 
Ideally, the Under 18 Head Coach will hold or have:
  • A minimum of 2 years’ coaching experience within the Professional Development Phase (U16–U21) at a Category 1 Academy.
  • Experience of leading or supporting the development of less experienced coaching staff.
  • Experience within the England Youth International pathway or equivalent representative football.
  • The FA Talent Identification Level 1 qualification.
  • A related higher education degree in coaching, analysis or sports science (or similar qualification).
  • Confidence, in the use of video/performance analysis platforms (e.g. HUDL or similar) to support individual player development.
  • Awareness of First Team environments and the holistic demands placed on elite level athletes.
  • Continuously demonstrates openness & inclusiveness.
  • Action orientated; solution focused.
  • Show pro-activeness and an ability to work around or overcome obstacles that others may find challenging.
  • Understand the importance of being a confident custodian for an organisation with history and tradition.

Requirements

The Under 18 Head Coach (‘U18 HC') is employed to prepare, deliver and review coaching activities in line with the Academy’s Performance Plan.
 
There is a specific requirement for the U18 HC to support individuals as they move into and through the Professional Development Phase by delivering on the agreed commitments within each players Individual Learning Plan (ILP) and leading the process of continual review and refinement supporting the programme to be suitably responsive to each individual’s dynamic needs.
 
This essentially makes the U18 HC responsible for the following, non-exhaustive list:
Preparing
  • Lead the creation and ongoing development of both Individual Learning Plans and the Age Group Plan for the U18s.
  • Play an active role in the transition of players from the U16 age group into the PDP, working closely with U16 coaching staff to ensure continuity of style, expectations and individual development priorities.
  • Lead and sustain frequent, consistent and supportive communication with all players and their families to support transitions into Professional Football.
  • Lead the Multi-Disciplinary Team to create seasonal, weekly and daily, team and individual training plans.
  • Lead the preparations of meaningful content for individual player (and parent) reviews.
  • Support the preparation of content for team and individual Performance Education, Physical Development and Psychology delivery, ensuring integration where possible.
  • Align video to team and individual commitments, supporting team and individual player development over time.

Delivering
  • Lead the delivery of team training sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan) specifically integrating team and individual outcomes into practice.
  • Lead the delivery of individual training sessions (both inside and outside of team training sessions) in line with ILP commitments.
  • Lead teams and individuals through fixtures, both home and away, as part of the age group games programme, ensuring we are appropriately competitive.
  • Lead teams and individuals through tours, tournaments and competitions aligning the environment design and coaching behaviours to the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan.
  • Lead the delivery of performance education sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan).
  • Support the delivery of the U16 and U21 programmes, as needed.
  • Attend first team games and youth international football events as required.
  • Oversee the implementation of the Academy Values and Behaviours towards staff and players.

Reviewing
  • Lead the effective review of team training sessions in line with ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan).
  • Lead the effective review of individual training sessions and their impact on player-coach relationships and player performance over time.
  • Review all team and individual match performances in all games programme, tours and tournament fixtures.
  • Coordinate the ongoing ‘rolling’ review of each player’s ILP, ensuring the creation of clear action plans, involving colleagues from different disciplinary backgrounds, through weekly MDT meetings.
  • Lead all player and parent review meetings, ensuring player and parent feedback is recorded and agreed actions are shared and followed up.
  • Ensure each player’s Performance Clock is up to date and accurate.
  • Ensure all players are provided with regular access to their personal performance data, highlighting key metrics in line with the Academy Technical Plan.
  • Support the feedback process for all trialists.

Leadership & Collaboration
  • Be an active role model for all Academy coaches across the pathway and wider Club environment.
  • Offer guidance and support to less experienced coaching colleagues, taking a specific and regular interest in the upper part of the YDP.
  • Act as a key point of connection between the U16 age group and the PDP, and support alignment between the U18 and U21 programmes.
  • Consistently demonstrate, and hold others to, the highest levels of professionalism.
  • Support the delivery of coach development events across the year, as required.
  • Be part of the Academy Technical Group, shaping the Technical Strategy for the long term.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Talent ID & Recruitment, support the retention and recruitment of Academy players, including feedback for trialists and identification of players ready to progress from the U16 age group.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Performance, coordinate the effective review of the physical development programme and performance of the age group fitness coach.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Insights, coordinate the effective review of the performance education programme and performance of the age group analyst.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on Friday 2nd October, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.
