job.title: Welfare Steward (Casual)
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

To provide support and assistance in managing Safeguarding, Accessibility and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) incidents at The City Ground on matchdays. This includes responding to concerns raised by supporters, offering appropriate guidance and support, and ensuring any incidents are handled sensitively, professionally and in line with Club policies and procedures. The role will help promote a safe, inclusive and welcoming matchday environment for all supporters, ensuring that any concerns are appropriately recorded, escalated and followed up where necessary.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Assist the Club in the effective, safe customer friendly management of matchdays and event days at the City Ground

  • Work in any area of the Stadium as directed by the Ground Safety Officer, Deputy Safety Officer or Stand Supervisor.

  • Attend Safeguarding, Accessibility or EDI related incidents within your designated location and resolve wherever possible, providing updates to the control room and completed incident reports post event.

  • Liaise with relevant departments relating to incidents where required.

  • Assist with supplying details in the event of an incident.

  • Assisting supporters with Accessibility requirements.

  • Ensure the radial gangway is kept clear.

  • Identify and report any potential safety issues.

  • Ensuring that the supervisor or relevant senior member of staff is alerted with appropriate information given.

  • Being a direct link between Safeguarding, EDI and match-day staff.

  • Assist with providing Supporter details to the Police upon request in line with our GDPR ‘data sharing agreement’.

  • To work consistently to embed and champion safeguarding, equality & diversity into the match-day experience.

  • Promote an inclusive, positive, supportive, and welcoming image of the club at all times.

  • Ensure compliance with the terms of the Club Safeguarding Policies and Procedures, Health and Safety Legislation and Club’s Equality Policy.

  • Support accessibility and inclusion on match days including accessible areas and multi-faith rooms.

  • Attend and respond to briefing and debriefing in relation to safety management and to report any matters of concern or interest to the Stand Supervisor Steward.

  • To undertake internal and/or external training including stewarding, Safeguarding, accessibility and EDI training required for the role as directed by the Club.

  • Any other reasonable duties and responsibilities which your manager or another senior officer of the Club asks you to perform.

What are we looking for:

  • Willingness to work in crowd management in a football environment

  • Good communication skills

  • Ability to deliver and maintain high levels of customer service

  • Knowledge and Experience around Safeguarding, Accessibility, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion.

  • Experience working within a Sporting Stadium

  • Previous Safeguarding experience with children and/or adults at risk

job.title: City Ground Facilities Manager
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Facilities and Maintenance

Reporting to: Head of Facilities

Closing Date For Applications: 20th November 2026

About the Role:

Based at The City Ground – the historic home of Nottingham Forest Football Club – this role will oversee all aspects of facilities management at the stadium, with a strong focus on cleaning services, waste management, and ensuring matchday hospitality areas, including the boardroom, are maintained to the highest possible standards.

The Facilities Manager will play a key role in delivering a first-class environment for supporters, staff, players, VIPs, and media, with specific responsibilities on home matchdays, ensuring the stadium is operationally ready and presented immaculately.

This role requires a proactive and hands-on leader, capable of managing a multi-disciplined team, including cleaners, maintenance staff, and external contractors. The successful candidate will be a visible presence on matchdays and throughout the week, ensuring that the facilities are clean, safe, compliant, and well maintained

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the day-to-day facilities management of The City Ground.

  • Lead and manage the cleaning team and contracted cleaning providers, ensuring all areas of the stadium, including public spaces, offices, changing rooms, and hospitality suites, meet high cleanliness standards.

  • Take full ownership of waste management processes, ensuring effective, safe, and sustainable disposal of waste across the stadium.

  • Deliver and uphold matchday readiness standards, including preparation and presentation of the boardroom, directors' box, VIP areas, and media zones.

  • Manage the stadium’s maintenance technician(s), ensuring that planned and reactive maintenance tasks are completed effectively.

  • Develop and manage a robust Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) schedule.

  • Monitor and manage maintenance and cleaning budgets,

  • ordering supplies and consumables as required, and reporting anomalies to the Head of Facilities.

  • Coordinate and supervise external contractors and service providers, ensuring compliance with club policies, safety standards, and work quality.

  • Conduct regular inspections and audits of stadium facilities, resolving issues proactively.

  • Maintain all required documentation and logs, including compliance records, contractor files, and safety certifications.

  • Lead on minor refurbishments and improvement projects at the stadium.

  • Support and contribute to club-wide environmental and sustainability initiatives.

  • Be present and operational for all home fixtures, including midweek and weekend games, and special events hosted at the stadium.

  • Support the wider facilities team with projects at other club sites (e.g., the Training Ground) as required

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • Previous experience in a facilities management role

  • Experience managing cleaning operations in a commercial or hospitality setting

  • Experience managing and leading teams

  • Strong knowledge of health & safety compliance, risk assessments, and contractor management

  • Full UK driving licence

Desirable:

  • Experience in a stadium or sports venue environment

  • Experience in the use of Halo event management software

  • Health & Safety qualification (e.g., IOSH, NEBOSH)

  • Experience leading capital works or minor refurbishment projects

job.title: Academy Safeguarding Manager
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Safeguarding

Reporting to: Head of Safeguarding

Closing Date For Applications: 27th November 2026

About the Role:

The designated person will have primary responsibility for leading and implementing the Academy's safeguarding strategy and policies and for putting excellent monitoring and reporting procedures into daily practice to safeguard children and adults at risk across the Academy.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Line Management of Academy Designated Safeguarding Officer.

  • Ensuring appropriate safeguarding cover at the training ground during all Academy activity.

  • Providing strategic influence and guidance on good safeguarding practise as part of the Academy Leadership Team.

  • Working with all stakeholders to create a positive, child-centred academy environment.

  • Lead on implementing and evolving the Academy’s approach to safeguarding children, young people and adults at risk.

  • Be the lead point of contact within the Academy for reporting and managing of Safeguarding concerns about children and young people and guide and delegate colleagues to manage concerns where appropriate.

  • Ensure all stakeholders are fully aware of reporting procedures through regular training and the dissemination of appropriate resources.

  • Manage cases relating to safeguarding concerns about children and young people reported to and by the Academy staff and stakeholders, undertake further investigations as/when required, and ensure all information is accurate, confidential, up to date, in line with GDP regulations and appropriately captured and monitored using our online system MyConcern.

  • Support the Head of Safeguarding to manage concerns relating to Academy staff when appropriate.

  • Liaise with parents/carers, schools, and local authorities when appropriate in relation to safeguarding concerns.

  • Maintain oversight of children and young people with additional vulnerabilities and ensure their needs are assessed and reasonable support is in place for them at the Academy.

  • Monitor and report on themes or trends in safeguarding matters at the Academy to the Academy Leadership Team, Head of Safeguarding and where appropriate the Senior Safeguarding Board.

  • Help to ensure that the Premier League standards are met within in the Academy by promoting and championing all safeguarding policy and procedures and assisting in compiling evidence for audits.

  • Develop policies, procedures and guidance documents to enhance safeguarding practises at the Academy. Facilitate and support the development and review of policies and procedures as appropriate.

  • Design and deliver educational interventions for staff including training, presentations, and resource materials to raise awareness of safeguarding policies, procedures, and guidance.

  • Design and regularly review the Academy safeguarding induction and ensure new starters receive relevant information and resources.

  • Support the Operations and Coaching departments with planning, preparing, and delivering trips and tours, including risk assessments and safeguarding provisions. Attend trips and tours on occasion to maintain oversight of risks, to assess safeguarding procedures, and to provide safeguarding support.

  • Assist the Academy in keeping staff’s safeguarding training up to date, including the FA Safeguarding Children certificates.

  • Support the Club’s safer recruitment process by ensuring new and existing staff undertake the relevant DBS checks in a timely manner.

  • Attend training and fixtures for all age groups in the Academy to observe and feedback where applicable on best practice. Including and not limited to training and fixture venues both home and away.

  • Provide advice and support to all staff, volunteers and associates of the organisation in relation to safeguarding concerns and queries.

  • Responsible for identifying staff training and development needs by evaluating strengths and weaknesses, Once identified, responsible for planning, organising and overseeing appropriate training on an annual basis.

  • Attend and contribute to Academy SWEP Group meetings as deemed appropriate.

  • Represent the Academy at Club safeguarding meetings and feedback where appropriate.

  • Maintain player information confidentiality and professional distance from all playing staff acting within professional codes of conduct and scope of practice at all times.

  • To act, at all times, in a manner appropriate to a representative of Nottingham Forest FC.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • FA Safeguarding Children or equivalent.

  • A recognised qualification in Player Care / Safeguarding.

  • Understanding of Safeguarding policies and procedures.

  • Experience of safeguarding and working with children, ideally in an elite sport environment.

  • Knowledge, understanding and experience of working with and supporting young people with mental health or wellbeing concerns.

  • Excellent presentation, planning and communication skills.

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills with the ability to multi-task and balance conflicting demands.

  • Experience in contributing to the design, delivery and evaluation of education and development interventions for individuals and groups.

  • Experience of working and contributing to a team environment by collaborating with others.

  • Ability to build strong relationships with players, parents, coaches and other stakeholders.

  • Ability to engage and communicate with people of all ages, especially young elite athletes.

  • Flexible, caring and a non-judgmental approach and attitude.

  • Always hold a professional manner and remain compliant with confidentiality.

  • Knowledge of roles and responsibilities of local statutory agencies (social services, police, and local safeguarding children board).

Desirable:

  • Previous experience in a safeguarding role in Academy football.

  • Mental Health First Aid training qualification.

  • FA Welfare Officer training.

Support the Head of Safeguarding to manage concerns relating to Academy staff when appropriate. - Liaise with parents/carers, schools, and local authorities when appropriate in relation to safeguarding concerns. - Maintain oversight of children and young people with additional vulnerabilities and ensure their needs are assessed and reasonable support is in place for them at the Academy. - Monitor and report on themes or trends in safeguarding matters at the Academy to the Academy Leadership Team, Head of Safeguarding and where appropriate the Senior Safeguarding Board. - Help to ensure that the Premier League standards are met within in the Academy by promoting and championing all safeguarding policy and procedures and assisting in compiling evidence for audits. - Develop policies, procedures and guidance documents to enhance safeguarding practises at the Academy. Facilitate and support the development and review of policies and procedures as appropriate. - Design and deliver educational interventions for staff including training, presentations, and resource materials to raise awareness of safeguarding policies, procedures, and guidance. - Design and regularly review the Academy safeguarding induction and ensure new starters receive relevant information and resources. - Support the Operations and Coaching departments with planning, preparing, and delivering trips and tours, including risk assessments and safeguarding provisions. Attend trips and tours on occasion to maintain oversight of risks, to assess safeguarding procedures, and to provide safeguarding support. - Assist the Academy in keeping staff’s safeguarding training up to date, including the FA Safeguarding Children certificates. - Support the Club’s safer recruitment process by ensuring new and existing staff undertake the relevant DBS checks in a timely manner. - Attend training and fixtures for all age groups in the Academy to observe and feedback where applicable on best practice. Including and not limited to training and fixture venues both home and away. - Provide advice and support to all staff, volunteers and associates of the organisation in relation to safeguarding concerns and queries. - Responsible for identifying staff training and development needs by evaluating strengths and weaknesses, Once identified, responsible for planning, organising and overseeing appropriate training on an annual basis. - Attend and contribute to Academy SWEP Group meetings as deemed appropriate. - Represent the Academy at Club safeguarding meetings and feedback where appropriate. - Maintain player information confidentiality and professional distance from all playing staff acting within professional codes of conduct and scope of practice at all times. - To act, at all times, in a manner appropriate to a representative of Nottingham Forest FC.
What are we looking for:
Essential:
- FA Safeguarding Children or equivalent. - A recognised qualification in Player Care / Safeguarding. - Understanding of Safeguarding policies and procedures. - Experience of safeguarding and working with children, ideally in an elite sport environment. - Knowledge, understanding and experience of working with and supporting young people with mental health or wellbeing concerns. - Excellent presentation, planning and communication skills. - Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills with the ability to multi-task and balance conflicting demands. - Experience in contributing to the design, delivery and evaluation of education and development interventions for individuals and groups. - Experience of working and contributing to a team environment by collaborating with others. - Ability to build strong relationships with players, parents, coaches and other stakeholders. - Ability to engage and communicate with people of all ages, especially young elite athletes. - Flexible, caring and a non-judgmental approach and attitude. - Always hold a professional manner and remain compliant with confidentiality. - Knowledge of roles and responsibilities of local statutory agencies (social services, police, and local safeguarding children board).
Desirable:
- Previous experience in a safeguarding role in Academy football. - Mental Health First Aid training qualification. - FA Welfare Officer training.
Forest For Everyone
We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.
Disability Confident Committed Employer
We are a Disability Confident Committed employer. We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.
If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to theEquality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via theDisability Confident Scheme- please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.
Our Commitment to Safeguarding
As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures
Health and Safety
Nottingham Forest is committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees, contractors, visitors, and guests. All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

job.title: Media Attendance Assistants
job.html_description:
We are looking for Media Attendance Assistants!

Job information
Division/Unit: Club Competitions Operations & Events
Contract type: maximum term
Start date: 01/03/2027
End date: 30/06/2027

Main goal

Your goal is to ensure the smooth journey of media stakeholders (press, photographers, video journalists, radio and TV non-rights holders) from their registration in the UEFA Media Channel, their media validation in the system, and eventually, accreditation and match booking requests to on-site attendance.

Key responsibilities

  • Overseeing the registration of bona fide Press, Photographers, Video Journalists, Radio & TV Non-Rights holders in the UEFA Media Portal
  • Ensuring an efficient accreditation and match booking media application process, in close liaison with UEFA ICT
  • Establishing documentation and standard operational processes that will be used by our counterparts, such as Press Officers, Onsite & Offsite staff, media representatives etc.
  • Coordinating the event-specific media stakeholders access needs with UEFA Accreditation and Access
  • Coordinating the media requests approval and rejection process with UEFA Communications as well as other internal stakeholders.
  • Answering the emails received from media representatives in a professional and client-centric approach
  • Assisting with the on-site delivery of media operations and services as required (Club and National Team Finals, Final Tournaments, Draws, etc.)
  • Applying the latest ICT developments to media services processes

Requirements

Experience:

  • Experience in event management where serving clients with high expectations is key and/or venue management in football or other sport
  • Good writing skills, including the ability to draft policies, guidelines and workflows

Education:

  • Bachelors' degree within the media environment, business management or sports/event management

Languages:

  • English / Advanced

Other requirements:

  • Knowledge of and interest in the sports media landscape in general, and particularly in football
  • Ability to provide outstanding results under pressure
  • Attention to details combined with the ability to see the big picture
  • The ability to work independently and reliably with precision and respecting confidentiality and multicultural concerns
  • A solution-oriented team player who is resilient, driven, amiable, energetic, diplomatic and charismatic with a positive outlook
  • Efficiency and the ability to keep track of numerous projects at once
  • Strong team spirit even in a high-pressure, changeable environment
  • Solid interpersonal skills with the ability to build a strong network
  • A creative and service-oriented mindset

Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

UEFA welcomes applications from all, actively working to ensure that we are an inclusive employer that finds the best candidate for our positions, regardless of aspects such as sex, gender identification, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity or nationality.

job.title: Media Rights and Broadcaster Services Intern
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: Marketing / Media Rights & Production Services
Contract type: Fixed term
Location: Nyon (up to one day working from home per week)
Start date: 15.01.2027
End date: 16.07.2027
Application deadline: 22.11.2026

Main goal

The Media Rights and Broadcaster Services Intern reports to the Media Rights Expert and supports the unit with the proper implementation of:

  • media rights strategies, ensuring revenue optimisation and a broad distribution platform for UEFA competitions;
  • communication with and information flows relating to UEFA’s broadcast partners (client-centric approach); and
  • unilateral broadcaster services for UEFA broadcast partners, including the allocation of resources, scheduling and general account management.

Key responsibilities

Licensing of archive footage

  • Handling daily archive licensing sales, servicing and contract management
  • Collaborating with colleagues in Legal and TV Production and externally with national associations, broadcasters, production companies and agencies as required
  • On completion of the internship: suggesting improvements to the overall process and strategy of UEFA’s direct archive footage sales

Media rights for youth, women's and futsal competitions

  • Providing administrative support to the Media Rights Expert in relation to the sale of the remaining rights to UEFA’s youth, women's and futsal competitions
  • Collecting information from national associations and redistributing it to relevant internal stakeholders as required

Unilateral broadcast services

Front office

  • Compiling and updating information from UEFA’s national team competitions agency (CAA Eleven) and other UEFA departments
  • Helping with administrative tasks
  • Providing general support with the account management of UEFA broadcast partners

Back office

  • Cross-checking documents and allocating services
  • Issuing operational reports
  • On completion of the internship: analysing the booking tool used by UEFA broadcast partners and providing recommendations for improvements

Requirements

Education:

  • Master's degree in business and/or marketing (completed or ongoing)

Languages:

  • English / Proficient
  • Any additional languages would be a plus

Other requirements:

  • Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected
  • MS Office / Proficient
  • Good understanding of football, especially the European game
  • Interest in the global media industry and related sports rights issues
  • Strong administrative skills
  • Good team spirit

Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

job.title: EURO Maps & Plans Assistant
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: UEFA Tournament Operations / Venue Operations
Contract type: Max-Term
Location: Nyon (WFH up to one day per week)
Start date: TBC
End date: 31/07/2028

Main goal

The Maps & Plans Assistant contributes to the development, quality control and distribution of technical plans, graphical maps and digital mapping solutions for UEFA events and tournaments, ensuring that mapping products are accurate, up to date and user-friendly. The successful candidate will help to prepare AutoCAD templates and clean and georeference base maps, while providing organisational and design support to the Maps & Plans team.

Key responsibilities

  • Supporting the Maps & Plans team with various tasks, in particular briefing reviews, quality control and map validation processes for both technical plans and graphical maps
  • Coordinating mapping-related requests from internal departments and external stakeholders, ensuring timely follow-up and delivery
  • Preparing and updating AutoCAD templates and facilities layouts for UEFA competitions, including club competition finals and UEFA EURO 2028
  • Cleaning and georeferencing architectural base maps for UEFA competitions
  • Helping to review technical plan and graphical map briefings
  • Assisting with last-minute updates and urgent map revisions as required
  • Assisting the team's graphic designer with the creation of design assets
  • Helping to maintain interactive and digital mapping solutions
  • Supporting communication between venue teams, suppliers and project managers regarding mapping deliverables

Requirements

Experience:

  • from 1 to 3 years experience in an international environment

    Education:

    • Bachelor's degree in architecture or equivalent

    Languages:

    • Fluent in English

    Other requirements:

    • Good organisational skills
    • Ability to spot and correct errors
    • Independent, versatile and proactive
    • High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy
    • Service-minded
    • Problem-solving and continuous improvement mindset
    • Excellent team player
    • Ability to cope with pressure and respect deadlines
    • Flexibility to work in dynamic event environments
    • Willingness to learn about UEFA operations

    Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

job.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Communications
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Manager, Corporate Communications supports and executes enterprise-wide communications strategies that build understanding, strengthen relationships, create meaningful opportunities for engagement and ensure U.S. Soccer’s Federation membership base feels informed, heard and connected to the organization’s mission and direction. In close partnership with the Senior Director of Corporate Communications and business partners across the Soccer Growth and Member Strategy teams, this role is responsible for developing and executing both internal and external communications plans and initiatives that reflect U.S. Soccer’s strategic priorities and mission. 


The ideal candidate is a strategic, proactive and relationship-driven communicator with experience navigating complex stakeholder environments and aligning messaging that helps members and key stakeholders including referees, coaches and youth leaders understand how the organizations work affects them. Areas of focus include executive communications, member engagement, and cross-functional coordination. 


This role oversees the development of executive briefing materials, talking points, background documents, and presentations for public appearances, media engagements, and internal leadership communications as it relates to Soccer Growth and Member Strategy initiatives. This role also supports larger Federation external functions, including board meetings, annual member meetings, annual general meetings of member organizations, regional meetings and public-facing appearances. 


Success in this role requires strong cross-functional collaboration, the ability to synthesize complex information for diverse audiences, and a commitment to ensuring that U.S. Soccer’s internal communications infrastructure and external messaging are aligned and mission-driven. 


Primary Responsibilities 

  • Develop and execute corporate communications strategies that support organizational priorities and strengthen reputation among members, partners, media and other stakeholders. 
  • Develop executive communications, talking points, presentations, messages and other materials for internal and external audiences. 
  • Identify opportunities to proactively tell the organization’s story and demonstrate its impact. 
  • Build strong relationships across departments and serve as a communications thought partner to teams working directly with members and stakeholders. 
  • Collaborate with marketing, digital, events, executive leadership, advancement and other teams to create integrated engagement strategies. 
  • Develop and lead integrated communications strategies that strengthen member understanding, connection and engagement with the organization. 
  • Build communications plans around major organizational initiatives, changes, announcements and priorities. 
  • Play a lead role in building a monthly membership newsletter. 
  • Establish meaningful measures of communications and member engagement effectiveness. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in corporate communications, media relations, membership communications or a related field, ideally within sports, entertainment, or nonprofit sectors.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field; advanced degree a plus. 
  • Strong understanding of the U.S. soccer ecosystem, including key stakeholders such as members, referees, coaches, and youth programs. 
  • Proven experience supporting C-suite executives with briefing materials, talking points, presentations, and internal/external messaging. 
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills across a variety of formats (speeches, memos, newsletters, social content, feature articles, etc.). 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive information and craft strategic responses in high-pressure or time-sensitive situations. 
  • Experience coordinating communications for high-profile events, such as board meetings, conventions, and internal town halls. 
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Ability to develop clear, consistent messaging across internal and external channels, aligned with organizational mission and voice. 
  • Comfort working collaboratively across departments and building relationships at all levels of an organization. 
  • Experience communicating with a membership, association, nonprofit or similarly diverse stakeholder base strongly preferred.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and travel up to two times per quarter. 
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). 

Desired Qualifications 

  • Strategic hustle, initiative, and work ethic with diversity of thought. 
  • Strong posture for empathy. 
  • Ability to build meaningful relationships both internally and externally. 
  • Able to think strategically and handle multiple projects. 
  • Confidence without ego. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus, but not required. 

 

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking a Sr. Coordinator, Media Operations to help deliver best-in-class media operations across the Federation’s 27 National Teams and major events, with a primary focus on the U.S. Men’s and Women’s National Teams.


Reporting to the Vice President, Communications, this role will be responsible for planning and executing media operations for National Team matches, camps, tournaments and other Federation events. The Sr. Coordinator will serve as a key operational contact for media and work closely with National Team press officers, Sporting, Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Commercial and venue partners to ensure media needs are thoughtfully planned and seamlessly executed.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable working in fast-paced, high-profile environments. This individual should understand the needs of working media, anticipate operational challenges and be able to independently manage multiple priorities and stakeholders while delivering a consistent, professional media experience.


The Sr. Coordinator will work cross-functionally with Communications, Sporting, Event Operations, Media, Security, Ticketing and venue partners to ensure media requirements are integrated into event planning and that U.S. Soccer delivers a consistent, professional media experience across its National Teams and events.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and execute media operations for U.S. Soccer National Team matches, camps, tournaments and Federation events, with primary focus on the Men’s and Women’s National Teams and support across all 27 National Teams as needed.
  • Manage media accreditation from application through event-day execution, including reviewing requests, assigning appropriate access, credential production and distribution, and troubleshooting accreditation issues.
  • Serve as a primary onsite point of contact for credentialed media, providing timely information, responding to questions and resolving operational issues.
  • Coordinate media facilities and operational requirements, including press boxes, media workrooms, press conference areas, mixed zones, photographer work areas and field-level positions, media entrances, connectivity, catering and other event-specific needs; manage photographer access and credential/bib distribution as required.
  • Manage media access and movement throughout venues, ensuring credentialed media are appropriately positioned, and event-specific access policies are followed.
  • Partner with venues and internal stakeholders in advance of matches and events to assess media infrastructure, determine operational needs and develop event-specific media operations plans; conduct pre-event walkthroughs and readiness checks to ensure media facilities, signage, technology and services meet established standards.
  • Partner closely with National and Youth Teams press officer to support player and coach media availability, live and virtual press conferences, training access and other team communications needs.
  • Develop and distribute media advisories and operational communications with accreditation details, schedules, access information, parking, media availability and other event logistics. Schedule virtual press conferences, provide links and meeting invites to all pertinent parties, and assist in execution.
  • Ensure U.S. Soccer Media Guidelines and event-specific access policies are consistently implemented, creating a professional working environment for journalists while protecting team needs and the rights of U.S. Soccer’s media partners.
  • Research local media markets and maintain accurate media lists and databases to support National Team and Federation communications efforts.
  • Build and maintain relationships with media operations contacts at venues, FIFA Member Associations, confederations and other soccer organizations.
  • Recruit, brief, train and manage event-day media volunteers, develop staffing plans and assignments, and establish clear roles, expectations and escalation procedures for each event.
  • Manage media operations equipment and inventory to ensure appropriate resources are available for National Team matches and events.
  • Manage media operations vendors, including sourcing services, negotiating agreements, tracking expenses and processing invoices within established budgets.
  • Collaborate with Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Ticketing, Commercial and other internal teams to ensure media requirements are incorporated into overall event planning.
  • Help develop and implement consistent media operations standards, processes and best practices across U.S. Soccer’s National Teams.
  • Support media operations planning and execution for major international tournaments and other high-profile events hosted or supported by U.S. Soccer.
  • Anticipate operational challenges and independently troubleshoot issues in real time during matches and events.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in media operations, communications, public relations, sports communications, event operations or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting media operations at major live sporting events; experience in professional or international soccer strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of media operations, accreditation and credentialing processes, venue access and the needs of working journalists, photographers and broadcasters.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage event logistics and multiple stakeholders in fast-paced, high-pressure environments.
  • Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, staffing plans, vendors and multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, solve problems and make decisions in live-event environments.
  • Strong service orientation and demonstrated ability to anticipate and respond to the needs of media and other event stakeholders.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple events, deadlines and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with media, athletes, coaches, executives, venue personnel and other high-profile stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with media accreditation, credentialing or event management platforms strongly preferred.
  • Spanish-language proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time and work nontraditional hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as needed.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Pro License Educator
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is looking for a Pro License Coach Educator to facilitate the U.S. Soccer Pro License and support the continued development of coaches working at the highest levels of the professional game. 


The ideal candidate combines significant experience in the professional game with expertise in player development and coach education. They understand the realities and demands of professional coaching and can create meaningful learning experiences that connect course learning with each student’s professional environment.


Working with the Pro License Technical Lead, this role will guide students through course learning, application in their club environments, feedback, reflection, and assessment. The Pro License Coach Educator will report to the Senior Director of Coaching Education and work closely with the Coach Education technical and operational staff, the Sporting Department, professional leagues and clubs, Coach Educators, mentors, and specialist contributors.


The role will also work closely with the Head of Continuous Professional Development to create and facilitate development opportunities that respond to the evolving needs of Pro-level coaches and the professional game


Primary Responsibilities

  

Pro License Course

  • Facilitate the Pro License curriculum across in-person and virtual learning experiences, mentoring, club visits, and application within students’ professional environments
  • Contribute to the continued improvement of the Pro License through insights from students, course delivery, research, and developments within the professional game

Student Learning & Development

  • Understand each student’s context, experience, strengths, and development needs
  • Build effective relationships and facilitate dialogue, reflection, and reality-based learning grounded in professional practices
  • Help students identify a development focus, apply learning in their club environment, gather evidence of their practice, and reflect on what they learn

Assessment & Mentoring

  • Observe professional practice, provide meaningful feedback, and support students and mentors
  • Document evidence of student learning and contribute to assessment and reassessment decisions in line with Pro License standards and processes
  • Contribute to consistency in assessment and Coach Educator practice across the Pro License

Player Development and the Professional Game

  • Bring current expertise in player development and the men’s and women’s professional game to connect individual and team development, game models, coaching processes, and performance demands
  • Adapt learning to the distinct player development, performance, and working environments across the men’s and women’s professional game
  • Ensure learning remains relevant to the evolving realities of professional soccer in the United States

Research, Innovation, and Continuous Professional Development

  • Stay current with research, innovation, emerging practice, and developments within the professional game
  • In collaboration with the Head of Continuous Professional Development, translate relevant research and emerging practice into meaningful development opportunities for Pro-level coaches   

Professional Partnerships

  • Build productive relationships across U.S. Soccer and with MLS, NWSL, USL, professional clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists
  • Use these relationships to strengthen learning, connect education with the professional game, and provide students with access to relevant expertise and professional environments

Professional Standards

  • Model the professional standards expected of U.S. Soccer Coach Educators, including safeguarding, inclusion, confidentiality, professional integrity, and responsible handling of student and club information

Requirements


Qualifications

  • Coaching Certification: U.S. Soccer Pro License or other confederation Pro License required
  • Education:  Bachelor’s degree in Coaching, Coach Education, Sport Science, High-Performance Coaching, Education, Adult Learning, or a related field preferred
  • Experience: Significant experience in professional coaching, technical leadership, player development, coach education, or high-performance environments.
  • Travel: Ability to travel nationally, conduct club visits, and work evenings and weekends when required by course delivery and the professional-game calendar.
  • Language: English required; Spanish proficiency is a plus
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States


Candidate Profile

We are looking for an experienced professional who can operate credibly across professional soccer and coach education. The successful candidate will bring:

  • Significant experience within professional soccer and a strong understanding of the realities and demands facing coaches, players, staff, and clubs
  • Deep expertise in player development and the ability to connect individual player development with team development, the game model, training, competition, and the wider performance environment
  • Current understanding of the men’s and women’s professional game in the United States, including MLS, NWSL, USL, their clubs, player pathways, competitive environments, and evolving coaching demands
  • Strong understanding of the women’s professional game and considerations relevant to female player development
  • Experience as a Coach Educator, including facilitating adult learning, mentoring coaches, observing professional practice, providing feedback, and contributing to assessment
  • Sound judgment in evaluating professional practice against defined standards, using evidence to support fair and consistent assessment
  • Ability to build trust and engage experienced professional coaches in meaningful dialogue, reflection, and learning
  • Curiosity about the game and a commitment to research, innovation, and continuous learning
  • Ability to translate research, emerging practice, and developments in the professional game into relevant learning experiences for coaches
  • Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across U.S. Soccer and with professional leagues, clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Case Administrator, Safeguarding
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is dedicated to safeguarding through creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for everyone involved in the game—especially players, coaches, referees, and volunteers. We work proactively to keep individuals with harmful intentions out of the soccer community through programs like Safe Soccer Clearance. We promote awareness and healthy behaviors across the sport to build a culture of well-being and safety. If harm or abuse occurs, we work to ensure it is identified, reported, and addressed quickly, appropriately, and with care for the survivor. Our goal is to maintain a system of policies, practices, and values that protect all participants—especially children and vulnerable individuals—from harm and abuse.


We are looking for a compassionate, detail-oriented, self-starter to join the small team of reporting and response professionals in our Safeguarding group as Case Administrator. The team processes a high volume of safeguarding-related reports each year, oftentimes directing reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, one of U.S. Soccer’s organization members, and/or law enforcement. The team also assists the organization with the administration of its Safe Soccer Clearance program by helping individuals appeal adverse participation or membership decisions made as a result of flags on their background screening. 


The Case Administrator plays a vital role in addressing complex and often emotionally challenging issues. The ideal candidate will bring not only a strong sense of purpose and commitment to the work, but also emotional intelligence, empathy, and resilience. Comfort with sensitive subject matter and the ability to engage thoughtfully and respectfully with diverse perspectives are essential for success in this role.


This is position reports to our Manager, Safeguarding Administration and is based at our National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA. The NTC offers a hybrid works schedule, with employees reporting to the office in person on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of each week. 


Primary Responsibilities


Background Screening Appeal Administration

  • Identify flagged screening reports and prepare them for review by an independent review panel
  • Identify screening reports that must be reported to the Center for SafeSport and/or law enforcement, and ensure that the organization’s mandatory reporting obligations are fulfilled
  • In consultation with the Manager, Safeguarding Administration and the SVP of Compliance & Safeguarding, communicate with U.S. Soccer’s background screening vendor on questions involving the organization’s flag matrix
  • Compile information from appellants to present to independent appeals panels, and coordinate the scheduling of live hearings
  • Educate appellants and organization members on the appeals process
  • Develop and maintain electronic case records

SafeSport Report Processing

  • Review reports received through U.S. Soccer’s reporting mechanisms
  • Refer reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, relevant organization members, and/or law enforcement where necessary and appropriate
  • Support organization members in navigating their reporting requirements and educate organization members on their response and resolution options
  • Respond to the Center for SafeSport’s information requests and communicate the Center for SafeSport’s notices and decisions to U.S. Soccer members
  • Update and maintain U.S. Soccer’s risk management list and the U.S. Soccer Learning Center’s disciplinary list
  • Develop and maintain electronic case records

U.S. Soccer recognizes that this role involves abuse reporting and that this is topic is upsetting and emotionally demanding. We are committed to supporting our Safeguarding team’s well-being. We foster a culture of openness and care, encouraging employees to speak up when they need support. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university is preferred, but commensurate experience will be considered. A degree in a human services-related field is preferred, but not required
  • 3-5 years of experience with case management (e.g. child and family services, insurance claims, protective services, social services, non-clinical case management) is a plus
  • Experience with safeguarding preferred, but not required
  • Experience working with case management software preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate with empathy, compassion, and emotional intelligence across a diverse range of individuals and stakeholders
  • Proven ability to navigate sensitive situations with tact, active listening, and thoughtful response
  • Ability to stay focused, juggle multiple things at once, and know what to prioritize
  • Displays a service-oriented mentality, with the ability to get things done on time, and respond to stakeholders’ needs with a sense of urgency
  • Ability to work independently but collaboratively with other members of the Safeguarding team
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive information 
  • Strong interpersonal skills, a positive attitude and the ability to communicate clearly and concisely both verbally and in writing
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

U.S. Soccer is dedicated to safeguarding through creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for everyone involved in the game—especially players, coaches, referees, and volunteers. We work proactively to keep individuals with harmful intentions out of the soccer community through programs like Safe Soccer Clearance. We promote awareness and healthy behaviors across the sport to build a culture of well-being and safety. If harm or abuse occurs, we work to ensure it is identified, reported, and addressed quickly, appropriately, and with care for the survivor. Our goal is to maintain a system of policies, practices, and values that protect all participants—especially children and vulnerable individuals—from harm and abuse.
We are looking for a compassionate, detail-oriented, self-starter to join the small team of reporting and response professionals in our Safeguarding group as Case Administrator. The team processes a high volume of safeguarding-related reports each year, oftentimes directing reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, one of U.S. Soccer’s organization members, and/or law enforcement. The team also assists the organization with the administration of its Safe Soccer Clearance program by helping individuals appeal adverse participation or membership decisions made as a result of flags on their background screening.
The Case Administrator plays a vital role in addressing complex and often emotionally challenging issues. The ideal candidate will bring not only a strong sense of purpose and commitment to the work, but also emotional intelligence, empathy, and resilience. Comfort with sensitive subject matter and the ability to engage thoughtfully and respectfully with diverse perspectives are essential for success in this role.
This is position reports to our Manager, Safeguarding Administration and is based at our National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA. The NTC offers a hybrid works schedule, with employees reporting to the office in person on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of each week.
Primary Responsibilities
Background Screening Appeal Administration
- Identify flagged screening reports and prepare them for review by an independent review panel - Identify screening reports that must be reported to the Center for SafeSport and/or law enforcement, and ensure that the organization’s mandatory reporting obligations are fulfilled - In consultation with the Manager, Safeguarding Administration and the SVP of Compliance & Safeguarding, communicate with U.S. Soccer’s background screening vendor on questions involving the organization’s flag matrix - Compile information from appellants to present to independent appeals panels, and coordinate the scheduling of live hearings - Educate appellants and organization members on the appeals process - Develop and maintain electronic case records
SafeSport Report Processing
- Review reports received through U.S. Soccer’s reporting mechanisms - Refer reports to the U.S. Center for SafeSport, relevant organization members, and/or law enforcement where necessary and appropriate - Support organization members in navigating their reporting requirements and educate organization members on their response and resolution options - Respond to the Center for SafeSport’s information requests and communicate the Center for SafeSport’s notices and decisions to U.S. Soccer members - Update and maintain U.S. Soccer’s risk management list and the U.S. Soccer Learning Center’s disciplinary list - Develop and maintain electronic case records
U.S. Soccer recognizes that this role involves abuse reporting and that this is topic is upsetting and emotionally demanding. We are committed to supporting our Safeguarding team’s well-being. We foster a culture of openness and care, encouraging employees to speak up when they need support.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university is preferred, but commensurate experience will be considered. A degree in a human services-related field is preferred, but not required - 3-5 years of experience with case management (e.g. child and family services, insurance claims, protective services, social services, non-clinical case management) is a plus - Experience with safeguarding preferred, but not required - Experience working with case management software preferred - Demonstrated ability to communicate with empathy, compassion, and emotional intelligence across a diverse range of individuals and stakeholders - Proven ability to navigate sensitive situations with tact, active listening, and thoughtful response - Ability to stay focused, juggle multiple things at once, and know what to prioritize - Displays a service-oriented mentality, with the ability to get things done on time, and respond to stakeholders’ needs with a sense of urgency - Ability to work independently but collaboratively with other members of the Safeguarding team - Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive information - Strong interpersonal skills, a positive attitude and the ability to communicate clearly and concisely both verbally and in writing - General knowledge of soccer - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.

job.title: Senior Manager, Donor Direct Marketing
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


Reporting to the Director, Annual Fund, the Senior Manager, Donor Direct Marketing leads the strategy, development, and execution of U.S. Soccer's Mass donor marketing and communications function.


This seat owns the mass audience segment of the donor file, meaning constituents making single gifts outside of a membership, from first gift through the mid-level entry point. It carries a revenue and donor target against that audience and grows it through an agency of record supplying direct mail, email, and paid digital. U.S. Soccer owns the thinking. The agency owns the making. This seat holds that line.


The work is to integrate a channel mix, build an entry ladder, and put a second gift behind every acquisition, and to establish the operating model, campaign calendar, attribution standard, and measurement discipline the program runs on. The Senior Manager also serves as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications.


Primary Responsibilities


The Mass Audience Program

  • Own the mass audience segment of the donor file and the FY27 revenue and donor targets committed against it, from acquisition and second gift through retention, reactivation, upgrade, and the transition into mid-level giving.
  • Design and execute the second gift program, build monthly recurring giving into every touch rather than running it as a standalone campaign, and lead retention and reactivation, moving reactivation from direct mail to email and paid digital.

Growth, Testing, and Channel Development

  • Build and run a rolling test plan across creative, offer, ask string, segment, and timing, each with a stated hypothesis and a read date, and move proven results into the standing program.
  • Expand digital reach and revenue through paid social, search, display, and connected TV, lookalike and retargeting audiences built off the donor file, and owned channels including the U.S. Soccer app, match day, and email.
  • Evaluate and launch new channels, platforms, and partners, including list and audience partnerships, digital fundraising platforms, and SMS, piloting each against a defined budget, target cost per donor, and decision point. Lead the first-year digital build: a low dollar acquisition pilot against the post World Cup file, and a triggered welcome and second gift series.

The Agency Program

  • Manage the agency of record relationship day to day, including the brief, creative review, calendar commitments, and accountability to committed revenue projections. Maintain the division of responsibility that keeps strategy, audience, offer architecture, segmentation, source coding, and copy approval in house while the agency delivers modeling, production, deployment, media buying, and matchback.
  • Manage media investment within the approved budget, including target cost per donor acquired, reallocation between channels, and the decision to discontinue an underperforming line. Lead the transition to the go-forward partner and recommend the ongoing mix of internal staff, agency scope, and shared Federation services.

The Campaign Calendar

  • Own the campaign calendar across the fiscal year and coordinate timing across the Federation so that appeals, the Fan Experience communications queue, and the membership renewal cycle do not collide.

Attribution and Measurement

  • Own attribution for the mass audience. Enforce the source coding standard on every touch, internal and agency, reproduce the agency matchback internally so that every campaign is read twice, and report cost per donor acquired, twelve-month value by acquisition source, response rate, average gift, and second gift rate.

Donor Communications and Storytelling

  • Own the message architecture across the donor journey, covering what each segment receives between asks as well as during them, and advance appeal messaging from a benefits framing to an impact framing themed against U.S. Soccer's philanthropic pillars.
  • Build the impact story intake process, drawing from Soccer Forward and the stewardship pipeline with rights and release status attached to each item, and own stewardship, acknowledgment, and impact reporting for the mass audience.

Cross-functional Partnership

  • Serve as Advancement's liaison to centralized Marketing & Communications on channel access, calendar position, brand approval, audience data, and message alignment.
  • Partner with Stewardship & Engagement, Advancement Services, Memberships, Major Gifts, and Principal Gifts on segmentation, gift attribution, and lifecycle transitions into and out of the mass audience, and with Corporate Partnerships on the match or challenge behind each pillar campaign.
  • Collaborate with Product, Digital, and Fan Experience on recurring giving capability, donation form performance, and the tracking required to attribute a gift to a specific appeal.
  • Support overall goals of the Advancement department.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in nonprofit direct response fundraising, integrated marketing, donor engagement, digital marketing, communications, advancement, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing multi-channel direct response programs across direct mail, email, and paid digital that drive donor acquisition, retention, and revenue growth.
  • Experience managing an agency or vendor relationship, including briefing creative, holding a partner to a campaign calendar, and evaluating performance against committed projections.
  • Experience building or significantly expanding donor marketing, fundraising communications, or audience engagement programs.
  • Experience designing and reading a testing program, including hypothesis, sample, and result, and carrying a proven test into the standing program.
  • Experience evaluating and launching new acquisition channels, platforms, or audience partnerships against a target cost per donor.
  • Working knowledge of fundraising analytics, including cost per donor acquired, donor value by acquisition source, response rate, and matchback methodology.
  • Strong understanding of donor lifecycle marketing, audience segmentation, source coding and attribution, and CRM-driven communications.
  • Proven ability to think strategically while leading complex campaigns from concept through execution.
  • Experience collaborating across fundraising, marketing, technology, digital, and communications teams within a complex organization.
  • Exceptional communication, storytelling, project management, and relationship-building skills with the ability to influence stakeholders across all levels of an organization.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and travel as needed.


Desired Qualifications

  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Experience supervising staff, agency teams, or cross-functional project teams.
  • Experience utilizing Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, email marketing systems, or comparable CRM and digital marketing technologies.



U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.
