job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


Reporting to the Director, Annual Fund, the Campaign Sr Coordinator owns the campaign calendar and the production behind it. This is a project management role with fundraising experience, accountable for moving every appeal, stewardship touch, and information moment from brief to drop, on schedule and correctly coded.


The calendar runs the full fiscal year and stays live rather than being rebuilt each quarter. Story intake sits with this seat as well, as a standing pull against programs across the Federation, banked with rights status attached so that a campaign brief begins from cleared evidence.


Primary Responsibilities


The Campaign Calendar 

  • Own the fiscal year campaign calendar covering every appeal, stewardship touch, and information moment, visible to every team that plans against it.
  • Confirm dates with Fan Experience, Membership, and Stewardship before they are committed.

Campaign Production

  • Run production from brief to drop across direct mail, email, and paid digital: creative routing, internal and legal approvals, proofs, data pulls, list and seed delivery, and drop dates.
  • Maintain the campaign brief as the single source of truth for audience, offer, ask string, timing, and creative direction, with a defined audience before work begins.
  • Run quality control before release, including proofing, link and donation path testing, personalization, and suppression verification, and maintain version control and archival so every campaign has a retrievable record of what dropped, to whom, and when.

Agency and Vendor Coordination

  • Hold the agency production schedule against ours and manage print, lettershop, data, and fulfillment vendors on timelines, postal drop windows, and delivery confirmation, escalating slipped dates before they affect a drop.

Story Intake and Content Operations

  • Build and run a standing story intake against Federation programs, maintaining a library of impact stories with rights, release, and usage status attached to each item.

Campaign Setup and Coding

  • Issue campaign IDs, source codes, and coded URLs against the U.S. Soccer source coding standard for every touch, internal and agency.
  • Set up campaigns in Salesforce and the email platform, including audience selections, tracking, and the records the program is reported from.

Cross-functional Partnership

  • Partner with Advancement Services on data pulls, segmentation delivery, suppression, and gift processing timelines.
  • Coordinate with Marketing & Communications, Fan Experience, Digital, and Product on channel access, calendar position, and brand approvals.
  • Support overall goals of the Advancement department.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 3+ years of project management or campaign production experience in nonprofit fundraising, direct response marketing, agency account management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multi-channel campaign production from brief through delivery, across direct mail, email, and digital.
  • Experience building and maintaining a production calendar across multiple concurrent campaigns and competing stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of direct mail production, including backward planning from the in-home date, proofing cycles, data and list processes, and postal timelines.
  • Experience coordinating agency or vendor deliverables against a schedule, including escalating slipped dates before they affect a drop.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, particularly in proofing, quality control, and version control.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to hold peers and partners to a deadline without direct authority over them.
  • Comfort documenting process and building a system where none exists.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and travel as needed.


Desired Qualifications

  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Experience utilizing Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, email marketing systems, or comparable CRM and digital marketing technologies.
  • Experience with source coding, campaign attribution, or marketing operations.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Counsel, Corporate Development
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer’s Corporate Development team leads inorganic growth initiatives to advance the organization’s strategic priorities and drive value creation. This includes mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments and partnerships, corporate integrations, and real estate development projects. The team works with cross-functional partners across U.S. Soccer, including Finance, Strategy, and Legal, to execute these projects. 


The Counsel, Corporate Development position is a new role at U.S. Soccer. Reporting to the Deputy General Counsel and embedded in the Corporate Development team, you will help us do the right thing the right way, make sound business decisions, manage risk, and creatively navigate internal and external challenges. 


You will provide general transactional support that is corporate in nature – think transactions involving mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments, real estate and financing, and bylaw amendments – and come to us with 4-6 years of corporate experience handling general corporate matters.  


This role can be in-person at our National Training Center in Fayetteville, Georgia (NTC) or  remote. If remote, occasional travel to the NTC and to member organizations’ offices is required to attend key meetings and build relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 


Primary Responsibilities

  • Support the legal structuring, negotiation, and execution of significant corporate transactions, including term sheets, letters of intent, managed services agreements, joint venture agreements, acquisition agreements, bylaw amendments, strategic alliance agreements, financing agreements, real estate-related agreements, and other transaction documentation.  
  • Perform legal due diligence for transactions, identifying legal, regulatory, and commercial risks and opportunities.  
  • Partner closely with leaders across Corporate Development, Legal, Risk Management, Compliance, and Finance to evaluate opportunities, structure transactions, and drive successful deal execution. 
  • Coordinate with outside counsel to ensure efficient, high-quality support on large transactions.  
  • Research and advise on transaction-related regulatory approval strategies. 
  • Prepare concise materials for executive leaders (and, as necessary, the Board of Directors) on transaction structure, key risks, and approval requirements.  
  • Support transaction integration and post-closing activities, including implementation of legal and governance requirements. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • J.D. from an accredited law school and an active license to practice law, in good standing, in at least one U.S. jurisdiction. 
  • 4–6 years of corporate legal experience, preferably at a top-tier law firm, with a significant focus on corporate transactions.   
  • Strong ability to translate complex legal and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for non-legal colleagues.
  • Exceptional drafting, negotiation, and analytical skills. 
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong commitment to quality work product, ethics, integrity, and compliance. 
  • Must be able to connect "micro" details to the "macro" vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with mergers and acquisitions, real estate transactions, and diligence is preferred. 
  • Prior experience managing transactions involving nonprofit organizations is desirable but not required. 
  • Sports industry experience is not required, but a general understanding of the youth soccer ecosystem in the United States is preferred. 


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.

job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Corporate Development team leads U.S. Soccer’s inorganic growth initiatives, advancing strategic priorities and creating long-term value for the Federation. Our work includes mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments / partnerships, integration planning and real estate development. We partner with teams across U.S. Soccer, including Finance, Strategy, and Legal to deliver on our projects. 


The Senior Manager, Transaction Execution is a core member of the Corporate Development team and will conduct due diligence, perform financial analyses, manage project workstreams, coordinate across Finance, Legal, HR, IT, Communications, and program teams, and prepare strategic discussion materials to drive key strategic transactions and initiatives at US Soccer. This role supports multiple concurrent transactions and serves as the day-to-day execution lead on each. 


Primary Responsibilities

  • Support the identification, evaluation, structuring, and execution of mergers, acquisitions, managed service agreements (MSAs), joint ventures, strategic investments, and partnerships. 
  • Build and maintain financial models and analyses, including transaction economics, funding and pro forma analyses, and scenario and sensitivity analyses. 
  • Run due diligence end to end across internal teams and external advisors, including managing data rooms, information requests, and issue tracking. 
  • Lead cross-functional working groups, gathering input from each function on how their areas will change and keeping them aligned through negotiation and signing. 
  • Provide project management for active transactions, including timelines, workplans, and status reporting across a portfolio of concurrent deals. 
  • Prepare memos, presentations, and other materials for Executive Leadership and Board discussions. 
  • Execute deals using the team’s standard templates and playbooks, and suggest improvements as gaps come up. 
  • As needed, conduct market and benchmarking research to support specific transactions. 
  • Contribute to special projects with Federation-wide impact.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field. 
  • 3 - 7 years of experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, transaction advisory, strategy consulting, or finance/corporate finance. 
  • Hands-on experience executing transactions, including financial modeling and due diligence. 
  • Strong analytical, valuation, and corporate finance skills. 
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders without direct authority. 
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex analysis into executive-ready materials. 
  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines across concurrent workstreams. 
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours as needed.
  • Able and willing to travel up to 30% of the year.
  • Must be able to connect "micro" details to the "macro" vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook).
  • Able to work from our National Training Center in Fayetteville, GA.

Desired Qualifications

  • MBA, CFA, or progress toward one. 
  • Experience in sports, media, nonprofit, or membership organizations.

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.

We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

The Corporate Development team leads U.S. Soccer’s inorganic growth initiatives, advancing strategic priorities and creating long-term value for the Federation. Our work includes mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments / partnerships, integration planning and real estate development. We partner with teams across U.S. Soccer, including Finance, Strategy, and Legal to deliver on our projects.


The Senior Director, Corporate Development will lead due diligence, deal negotiations, structuring, and manage internal and Board approvals for potential mergers, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and joint ventures, with a particular focus on US Soccer’s player pathway and regional/local model strategy. This leader will own a portfolio of transactions end to end, collaborating with cross functional teams at US Soccer and external stakeholders including State Associations and other regional and local soccer organizations.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain the transaction strategy and pipeline for regional/local model strategy, aligned with the U.S. Soccer’s strategic priorities.
  • Lead deal structuring and negotiation of key terms across multiple concurrent transactions, working closely with Legal and outside counsel through definitive documentation and close.
  • Direct financial, commercial, people, operational, and legal due diligence, coordinating internal workstreams and external advisors.
  • Oversee financial models and analyses, including transaction economics, funding, pro formas, and scenario analyses.
  • Build repeatable templates, playbooks, and trackers that standardize the process across similar transactions.
  • Identify, quantify, and mitigate transaction risks.
  • Hand off diligence findings and commitments to the integration team to support integration planning.
  • Direct and mentor deal team members within the Corporate Development team.
  • Lead special projects with Federation-wide impact as needed.
  • Prepare strategic discussion materials for Executive Leadership and the Board decision making.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, strategy consulting, or finance/corporate finance, including significant experience leading transactions from origination through close.
  • Demonstrated success negotiating and structuring M&A, joint venture, or strategic partnership transactions.
  • Proven ability to lead teams and manage multiple complex workstreams and external advisors at once.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the judgment to navigate sensitive negotiations and stakeholder relationships.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours as needed.
  • Able and willing to travel up to 30% of the year.

Desired Qualifications

  • MBA, CFA, or other advanced degree.
  • Experience in sports, nonprofit, membership, or federated organizations, or with multi-site roll-up transactions.
  • Familiarity with the U.S. youth and amateur soccer landscape.
  • Experience negotiating with member-led or volunteer-governed boards.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.Position DescriptionThe Regional Refereeing Lead – West leads U.S. Soccer’s refereeing development activity across the West region and serves as the primary link between U.S. Soccer’s national refereeing strategy and regional delivery.The role works closely with State Referee Committees, local referee organizations, competition partners, referee coaches, and other regional stakeholders to strengthen referee development, support consistent delivery of national programs, and provide a visible and connected U.S. Soccer presence across the region.The West Region includes engagement with the State Referee Committees serving Alaska, Arizona, California North, California South, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.The position supports the regional delivery of national refereeing programs across education, coaching, evaluation, referee safety, talent identification, and development. This includes leading the regional delivery of R90+ and ensuring the program is effectively connected to the wider referee development pathway.The Regional Refereeing Lead builds strong relationships across the region, supports State Referee Committees and local organizations in implementing national priorities, and brings regional insight directly into how refereeing programs are designed, refined, and delivered.The position coordinates referees, coaches, and development activity across matches, coaching touchpoints, assessments, and regional events, ensuring a consistent and practical approach to referee development.The Regional Refereeing Lead also contributes to talent identification and progression by providing performance insight, observations, and recommendations to support national decision-making.Working closely with national refereeing staff and fellow Regional Refereeing Leads, the position ensures regional delivery aligns with national standards while helping shape how national programs evolve. The role brings a clear view of regional activity, emerging talent, development needs, challenges, and opportunities into national planning and decision-making.  As U.S. Soccer’s refereeing voice in the West, the Regional Refereeing Lead must be an exceptional communicator. This person explains national direction clearly in writing and in person, presents confidently to audiences ranging from volunteer referees to state leadership, and can deliver difficult or unpopular decisions while keeping the trust and credibility of the people affected.Primary ResponsibilitiesBuild and maintain strong working relationships with State Referee Committees, local referee organizations, competition partners, and regional programs to support alignment with U.S. Soccer refereeing strategy.Serve as a key U.S. Soccer refereeing development contact for State Referee Committees across the West, maintaining regular engagement, understanding regional needs, and supporting implementation of national initiatives.Support the regional delivery of national programs across referee education, coaching, evaluation, referee safety, talent identification, and development.Gather structured feedback from regional stakeholders and work with national staff to shape the design, refinement, and rollout of refereeing programs, bringing a regional perspective into national planning rather than reporting on delivery.Collaborate with peer Regional Refereeing Leads to share effective practice, align delivery and coaching standards, coordinate cross-regional opportunities such as shared events and referee exchanges, and ensure a consistent national experience for referees and coaches.Coordinate regional referee development activities across matches, coaching touchpoints, assessments, and events to support continuous development.Lead the regional delivery of R90+, ensuring alignment with national standards, structure, and expectations.Support the ongoing development of R90+ participants through coaching, development planning, match opportunities, regional events, and performance tracking.Lead and coordinate the regional coaching network, working with stakeholders to allocate coaches, oversee delivery, and maintain consistent coaching standards.Coordinate and guide the assignment of referees to appropriate development matches, events, and opportunities, aligning activity to referee readiness and program objectives.Build relationships with regional competitions and events to create appropriate development, observation, coaching, and talent identification opportunities for referees.Ensure regional referee development activity is accurately captured within U.S. Soccer’s referee intelligence platforms, supporting consistent tracking, accurate data, and effective use of insights.Identify and monitor referees with potential for progression, providing performance data, observations, and recommendations to support national selection and advancement decisions.Maintain a clear view of referee and coach development across the West and provide regular insight to national staff on regional activity, emerging talent, development needs, risks, and opportunities.Act as the primary voice of U.S. Soccer refereeing in the West, communicating national programs, priorities, and decisions through written updates, presentations, and direct conversations, including explaining difficult or unpopular decisions in a way that maintains trust and credibility.Work with operational teams to support the effective planning and delivery of regional events and development activity.

design, refinement, and rollout of refereeing programs, bringing a regional perspective into national planning rather than reporting on delivery.Collaborate with peer Regional Refereeing Leads to share effective practice, align delivery and coaching standards, coordinate cross-regional opportunities such as shared events and referee exchanges, and ensure a consistent national experience for referees and coaches.Coordinate regional referee development activities across matches, coaching touchpoints, assessments, and events to support continuous development.Lead the regional delivery of R90+, ensuring alignment with national standards, structure, and expectations.Support the ongoing development of R90+ participants through coaching, development planning, match opportunities, regional events, and performance tracking.Lead and coordinate the regional coaching network, working with stakeholders to allocate coaches, oversee delivery, and maintain consistent coaching standards.Coordinate and guide the assignment of referees to appropriate development matches, events, and opportunities, aligning activity to referee readiness and program objectives.Build relationships with regional competitions and events to create appropriate development, observation, coaching, and talent identification opportunities for referees.Ensure regional referee development activity is accurately captured within U.S. Soccer’s referee intelligence platforms, supporting consistent tracking, accurate data, and effective use of insights.Identify and monitor referees with potential for progression, providing performance data, observations, and recommendations to support national selection and advancement decisions.Maintain a clear view of referee and coach development across the West and provide regular insight to national staff on regional activity, emerging talent, development needs, risks, and opportunities.Act as the primary voice of U.S. Soccer refereeing in the West, communicating national programs, priorities, and decisions through written updates, presentations, and direct conversations, including explaining difficult or unpopular decisions in a way that maintains trust and credibility.Work with operational teams to support the effective planning and delivery of regional events and development activity.

job.title: Director, Prospect Development & Strategy
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

Reporting to the Senior Director, Advancement Services, the Director, Prospect Development & Strategy will build and lead U.S. Soccer's prospect development and fundraising strategy capabilities, establishing the frameworks, practices, and fundraising discipline needed to support an Advancement program raising $70M+ annually and scaling toward $100M.


Serving as a strategic partner to Advancement leadership and frontline fundraisers, the Director will bring deep fundraising expertise and relationship-management practices to prospect identification, portfolio strategy, pipeline development, and moves management. With particular emphasis on principal, transformational, and complex philanthropic opportunities, this role will help fundraisers identify the strongest pathways to advance donor relationships and drive philanthropic growth.


In partnership with the Senior Director, Advancement Services, the Director will lead the development of prospect and portfolio management capabilities within Salesforce, embed U.S. Soccer's frontline fundraising methodology into daily practices, and oversee the growth and effectiveness of the prospect development function.


We’d love to learn more about you—please include a brief cover letter sharing why you’re excited about this role and what you’d bring to the team. 


Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead a comprehensive prospect development strategy aligned with U.S. Soccer's fundraising priorities, campaign objectives, and long-term philanthropic growth.
  • Build and scale prospect development capabilities by establishing the strategic roadmap, operating framework, performance measures, and resources needed to support a growing Advancement program.
  • Partner across Major Gifts, Principal Gifts, Annual Fund, Institutional Giving, Stewardship, and Advancement leadership to align prospect development strategy, fundraising priorities, pipeline growth, and relationship-management practices.
  • Partner with fundraising leadership to develop and advance strategies for principal, transformational, stalled, and complex philanthropic opportunities, identifying relationship dynamics, barriers, strategic connections, and next actions.
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to leadership and frontline fundraisers on relationship and account strategy, cultivation, solicitation planning, and opportunity progression.
  • Lead the design and implementation of a comprehensive moves-management program, establishing clear definitions, business rules, and milestones for prospect qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and ongoing relationship management.
  • Establish portfolio and pipeline management standards, including qualification criteria, portfolio composition, assignment and reassignment practices, capacity expectations, opportunity stages, aging standards, and next-action requirements. Lead regular portfolio and pipeline reviews that strengthen accountability and advance donor relationships.
  • Establish strategic priorities and expectations for prospect identification, research, screening, and qualification, ensuring research produces timely, actionable intelligence that supports fundraising strategy and leadership-level giving.
  • Partner with fundraisers and leadership to translate prospect intelligence into recommendations for prioritization, relationship strategy, assignments, and next actions that advance qualified prospects through the pipeline.
  • Lead, supervise, mentor, and develop the Manager, Prospect Research & Management, overseeing the effectiveness and growth of the research function and assessing future staffing and resource needs.
  • Lead the implementation and adoption of U.S. Soccer's frontline fundraising methodology, including Plus Delta, integrating relationship-management practices into fundraising strategy, coaching, portfolio management, and pipeline reviews.
  • Help lead the definition of business requirements for prospect development and management capabilities within Salesforce, including functional requirements, workflows, data standards, and processes that support frontline fundraising and drive adoption.
  • Monitor portfolio and pipeline health, prospect movement, qualification effectiveness, and adoption of established practices to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Support the strategic priorities and growth of the Advancement department and perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in prospect development, major/principal gift fundraising strategy, advancement leadership, relationship/account management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience building, transforming, or significantly scaling a prospect development, fundraising strategy, or relationship-management function.
  • Deep understanding of major and principal gift fundraising best practices, including qualification, portfolio and pipeline management, moves management, cultivation, solicitation, and relationship strategy.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and advising on strategies for principal, transformational, and complex philanthropic opportunities, including high-capacity donor engagement, relationship mapping, and solicitation planning.
  • Proven ability to serve as a strategic partner to senior Advancement leadership and frontline fundraisers, translating research, data, and relationship intelligence into actionable fundraising strategies and coaching fundraisers on opportunity progression.
  • Experience designing and implementing portfolio, pipeline, qualification, and moves-management frameworks within a complex fundraising or relationship-driven organization.
  • Experience translating fundraising strategy and business requirements into CRM processes and functionality; experience implementing prospect management capabilities in Salesforce or a comparable CRM strongly preferred.
  • Experience implementing fundraising methodologies or significant changes in frontline practices and driving adoption; familiarity with Plus Delta or similar relationship-based fundraising methodologies preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience hiring, supervising, coaching, and developing professional staff, including building team capabilities and establishing clear performance expectations.
  • Exceptional strategic thinking, facilitation, coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior leadership and work effectively across functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change, establish new processes and operating practices, and balance strategic planning with hands-on implementation.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • General knowledge of soccer preferred.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.
